lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oof, I'm finally here! At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One! ;)
lines.script: [weary, relieved] Oof, I'm finally here! [dry, pleased] At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One! ;)

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA! You're BACK!
lines.script: [squealing, delighted] TAH TAH! You're BACK!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We waited for you for a hundred years.
lines.script: [dramatic, bossy] We waited for you for a hundred years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A hundred MILLION years!
lines.script: [loud, silly] A hundred MILLION years!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, up! Up up up!
lines.script: [eager, demanding] Tah Tah, up! [insistent, bright] Up up up!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm the tallest! Giddyup, Tata!
lines.script: [triumphant, giggly] I'm the tallest! [bossy, silly] Giddyup, Tah Tah!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Rose. Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Hello, Rose. [mock formal] Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, LOOK. A sparkling diamond gold dumpling squishy!
lines.script: [thrilled, hushed] Tah Tah, LOOK. [reverent, bright] A sparkling diamond gold dumpling squishy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's limited edition. There are only two in the whole world. You can squeeze it!
lines.script: [smug, proud] It's limited edition. [dramatic, hushed] There are only two in the whole world. [generous, bright] You can squeeze it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the shiniest dumpling I've ever seen. And I've seen a LOT of dumplings.
lines.script: [dry, impressed] That's the shiniest dumpling I've ever seen. [deadpan, flat] And I've seen a LOT of dumplings.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Come on, Tata! Let's go!
lines.script: [eager, giddy] Come on, Tah Tah! Let's go!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Deedee made rhubarb crisp for you. It's cooling RIGHT NOW.
lines.script: [excited, bossy] Tah Tah! Deedee made rhubarb crisp for you. [eager, emphatic] It's cooling RIGHT NOW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I already licked the spoon. Don't tell.
lines.script: [guilty, whispering] I already licked the spoon. [conspiratorial, hushed] Don't tell.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we had better hurry. Before somebody licks the rest.
lines.script: [dry, calm] Then we had better hurry. [deadpan] Before somebody licks the rest.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There's my Tom!
lines.script: [warm, overjoyed] There's my Tom!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And my girls! Come here, come here.
lines.script: [bustling, loving] And my girls! [coaxing, fussing] Come here, come here.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you're skin and bones. Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.
lines.script: [warm, fussing] Tom, you're skin and bones. [brisk, firm] Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Where are my reading glasses? I had them one second ago. I need to read the timer.
lines.script: [flustered, distracted] Where are my reading glasses? [muttering, puzzled] I had them one second ago. [impatient, fussing] I need to read the timer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. They're on your head.
lines.script: [flat, patient] Deedee. They're on your head.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: So they are. Not one word to Boppy.
lines.script: [sheepish, caught] So they are. [low, conspiratorial] Not one word to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I brought you a sourdough loaf. Baked it yesterday. It flew here on my lap.
lines.script: [dry, proud] I brought you a sourdough loaf. Baked it yesterday. [deadpan] It flew here on my lap.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. Now THAT is a meal.
lines.script: [delighted, warm] Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. [satisfied, emphatic] Now THAT is a meal.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A sliver for me. Just a sliver. Sourdough gives me gas.
lines.script: [casual, bargaining] A sliver for me. Just a sliver. [matter-of-fact, mild] Sourdough gives me gas.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, EVERYTHING gives you gas.
lines.script: [deadpan, exasperated] Mom, EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And I eat it anyway. That's love, Tom.
lines.script: [unbothered, tender] And I eat it anyway. [warm, fond] That's love, Tom.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom! Good. I'm not feeling good. It's the stomach.
lines.script: [grumbling] Tom! Good. I'm not feeling good. [pained] It's the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! A mud blob is taking your PIE!
lines.script: [alarmed, breathless] Deedee! [shrill, urgent] A mud blob is taking your PIE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!
lines.script: [outraged, dry] That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my GOOD tin! Grab your shoes. I'm coming with you.
lines.script: [outraged, fierce] That's my GOOD tin! [commanding, brisk] Grab your shoes. I'm coming with you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I TOLD you something lives in that pond. Twenty years I've been saying it. Nobody listens to Boppy.
lines.script: [aggrieved, vindicated] I TOLD you something lives in that pond. [tired, huffy] Twenty years I've been saying it. [sulky] Nobody listens to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'd come, but the stomach. Bring me back that fish.
lines.script: [pained] I'd come, but... the stomach. [brighter] Bring me back that fish.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Crumbs! Rhubarb crumbs. That little thief went right through here.
lines.script: [brisk, keen] Crumbs! Rhubarb crumbs. [indignant, fussing] That little thief went right through here.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. The mud is MOVING.
lines.script: [hushed, alarmed] Tah Tah. [whispering, urgent] The mud is MOVING.

lines.speaker: Mudling
lines.text: Blub. The pie went that way. You can't have it. Blub.
lines.script: [sulky, gloopy] Blub. The pie went that way. [petulant, stubborn] You can't have it. Blub.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Okay, everybody. Tata is in front. I'm in charge of choreography. FIGHT!
lines.script: [bossy, commanding] Okay, everybody. Tah Tah is in front. I'm in charge of choreography. [shrill, rallying] FIGHT!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.
lines.script: [soothing, tender] Up, up. Everybody up. [warm, cooing] Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.
lines.script: [brisk, fond] There. Good as new. [mock stern] Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Good job, girls. The crumbs keep going north.
lines.script: [proud, brisk] Good job, girls. [focused, cheerful] The crumbs keep going north.

lines.speaker: Skeeter Swarm
lines.text: Bzzz. Somebody smells like rhubarb. Bzzzzz.
lines.script: [thin, whiny] Bzzz. Somebody smells like rhubarb. [leering, delighted] Bzzzzz.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ew. Ew ew ew. Nobody touch my hair.
lines.script: [disgusted, shrill] Ew. Ew ew ew. [bossy, panicked] Nobody touch my hair.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Everybody okay? Itchy isn't hurt. Keep walking.
lines.script: [brisk, calm] Everybody okay? Itchy isn't hurt. [firm, cheerful] Keep walking.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: Grrrumble. You're standing in my puddle. And the small one is LAUGHING at me.
lines.script: [low, gravelly] Grrrumble. You're standing in my puddle. [cranky, wounded] And the small one is LAUGHING at me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm not laughing. I'm giggling. It's different.
lines.script: [indignant, earnest] I'm not laughing. I'm giggling. [prim, serious] It's different.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: That's IT. Soggy Slap. For the giggler.
lines.script: [furious, gravelly] That's IT. [spiteful, relishing] Soggy Slap. For the giggler.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hugs for everyone. There. All better.
lines.script: [warm, soothing] Hugs for everyone. [tender, soft] There. All better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The crumbs go around the pond. Toward Boppy’s fishing spot.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] The crumbs go around the pond. [knowing, warm] Toward Boppy’s fishing spot.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy says the Big One lives over there.
lines.script: [helpful, matter-of-fact] Boppy says the Big One lives over there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy also says the stomach thing is serious. Stay close.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Boppy also says the stomach thing is serious. [warm, low] Stay close.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: THERE! The thief! He still has the tin!
lines.script: [shouting, triumphant] THERE! The thief! [indignant, shrill] He still has the tin!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: GLUB. Is that a pie? For me?
lines.script: [booming, delighted] GLUB. Is that a pie? [childlike, thrilled] For me?

lines.speaker: Big Mudling
lines.text: Blub. For you, boss.
lines.script: [small, eager] Blub. For you, boss.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: It fits. I'm a king now. GLUB.
lines.script: [pompous, smug] It fits. I'm a king now. [gleeful, bubbling] GLUB.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!
lines.script: [furious, scolding] That's my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, he looks like a turtle wearing a hat.
lines.script: [whispering, delighted] Tah Tah, he looks like a turtle wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody touches Deedee’s crisp. Everybody ready?
lines.script: [dry, protective] Nobody touches Deedee’s crisp. [steady, calm] Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.
lines.script: [brisk, commanding] Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. [bright, encouraging] Rosie, make it laugh. [firm, warm] Then we try again.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Nobody ever made me laugh before. You can have your tin back.
lines.script: [stunned, bubbling] Glub. Nobody ever made me laugh before. [grudging, soft] You can have your tin back.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Fine. Take your tin. I'm going back in the pond to think about things.
lines.script: [sulky, gravelly] Glub. Fine. Take your tin. [mumbling, sheepish] I'm going back in the pond to think about things.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My tin! And look. Half the crisp is still in it.
lines.script: [delighted, relieved] My tin! [fussing, brighter] And look. Half the crisp is still in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The Big One ate the other half. I saw crumbs on its chin.
lines.script: [smug, matter-of-fact] The Big One ate the other half. [triumphant, bright] I saw crumbs on its chin.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then we split this half. Everybody home. Boppy has to hear about this.
lines.script: [brisk, generous] Then we split this half. Everybody home. [eager, bustling] Boppy has to hear about this.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You found the Big One? I TOLD everybody. Twenty years.
lines.script: [eager, vindicated] You found the Big One? I TOLD everybody. [wistful] Twenty years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It had this stuck in its lip.
lines.script: [dry, casual] It had this stuck in its lip.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My LURE! I lost that in 2006. Still shiny. Unlike me.
lines.script: [shocked, delighted] My LURE! I lost that in 2006. [wry] Still shiny. Unlike me.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Keep it, Tom. For luck. The fish clearly didn't want it.
lines.script: [generous] Keep it, Tom. For luck. [dry, amused] The fish clearly didn't want it.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Sit. Everybody sit. Half a crisp is still a crisp.
lines.script: [warm, bossy] Sit. Everybody sit. [fond, practical] Half a crisp is still a crisp.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: This is the best half a crisp I ever had.
lines.script: [blissful, sincere] This is the best half a crisp I ever had.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you're staying the WHOLE week, right?
lines.script: [hopeful, bossy] Tah Tah, you're staying the WHOLE week, right?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The whole week. And nobody is stealing anything else.
lines.script: [warm, steady] The whole week. [dry, mock stern] And nobody is stealing anything else.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Slow down. Everybody eats too fast. My stomach.
lines.script: [grumbling] Slow down. Everybody eats too fast. [pained] My stomach.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft. He's never home.
lines.script: [dry, mild] TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft. [flat, resigned] He's never home.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...He said he'd be home.
lines.script: [puzzled, hopeful] ...He said he'd be home.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.
lines.script: [smooth, amused] Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew three thousand miles to see you. The starter is the bonus.
lines.script: [dry, warm] I flew three thousand miles to see you. [deadpan, wry] The starter is the bonus.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Main event. I'll take it. Sounds premium. Like your seat.
lines.script: [amused, easy] Main event. I'll take it. [teasing, smug] Sounds premium. Like your seat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My call time got pushed to Thursday. The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. So I'm all yours.
lines.script: [easy, wry] My call time got pushed to Thursday. [deadpan, casual] The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. [warm, soft] So I'm all yours.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, something is up. The sky over Griffith Park went purple this morning. Not sunset purple. Weird purple.
lines.script: [easy, uneasy] Also, something is up. [low, puzzled] The sky over Griffith Park went purple this morning. [dry, unsettled] Not sunset purple... Weird purple.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: All yours. I like that. We'll look, together. One quick stop first. My starter has been alone for a week.
lines.script: [soft, pleased] All yours. I like that. [calm, steady] We'll look, together. [dry, sheepish] One quick stop first. My starter has been alone for a week.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Olivia dropped her off this morning. Family trip to the desert. No dogs at the hotel.
lines.script: [easy, warm] Olivia dropped her off this morning. [easy, matter-of-fact] Family trip to the desert. [dry] No dogs at the hotel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's been sitting on your porch since eight. I tried to take her to the loft. She refused.
lines.script: [easy, amused] She's been sitting on your porch since eight. [dry, rueful] I tried to take her to the loft. [deadpan] She refused.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it. Don't be mad.
lines.script: [easy, sheepish] Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it. [quick, coaxing] Don't be mad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mad? I'm proud. And a little mad.
lines.script: [dry, mock-offended] Mad? I'm proud. [deadpan, grudging] And a little mad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. Very polite. Very strong paw.
lines.script: [dry, fond] Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. [deadpan, proud] Very polite. Very strong paw.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Bready Mercury. Did you miss me? You missed me.
lines.script: [tender, cooing] Hello, Bready Mercury. [warm, teasing] Did you miss me? You missed me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles. Proud of you.
lines.script: [focused, murmuring] Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. [soft, delighted] Look at those bubbles. [warm, proud] Proud of you.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You talk to that jar more than you talk to me.
lines.script: [easy, teasing] You talk to that jar [mock-wounded, dry] more than you talk to me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The jar gets fifty grams of flour. You get the whole week.
lines.script: [dry, steady] The jar gets fifty grams of flour. [warm, sincere] You get the whole week.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...And you steamed my shirts for the flight. You win. You always win.
lines.script: [soft, trailing] ...And you steamed my shirts for the flight. [tender, fond] You win. You always win.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'll take it.
lines.script: [easy, pleased] I'll take it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look outside. Is the street... purple?
lines.script: [easy, puzzled] Babe. Look outside. [slow, uneasy] Is the street... purple?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington! Is everything okay?
lines.script: [calling, concerned] Mr. Washington! [gentle, worried] Is everything okay?

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Tom. Back in 1979, this whole block...
lines.script: [slow, dreamy] Tom. [wistful, drifting] Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.script: [faint, vacant] ...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.script: [faint, vacant] ...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.script: [faint, vacant] ...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.script: [faint, vacant] ...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.script: [faint, vacant] ...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He's been on "this whole block" for a while, babe.
lines.script: [low, dry] He's been on "this whole block" for a while, babe.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon.
lines.script: [dreamy, serene] Such a nice afternoon. [soft, drawn out] It should ALWAYS be this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, smog. That was UNCALLED for.
lines.script: [dry, indignant] Excuse me, smog. [sharp, outraged] That was UNCALLED for.

lines.speaker: Smoglet
lines.text: Cough. Nice street. We're going to sit on it for a while. Forever, actually.
lines.script: [wheezy, smug] Cough. Nice street. [lazy, menacing] We're going to sit on it for a while. [gleeful, wheezy] Forever, actually.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Remember movie night? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.
lines.script: [easy, teasing] Babe. Remember movie night? [dry, amused] You threw the whole popcorn bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was startled. Briefly. With dignity.
lines.script: [dry, defensive] I was startled. Briefly. [lofty, deadpan] With dignity.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It was a battle plan. You just didn't know it yet.
lines.script: [easy, playful] It was a battle plan. [warm, teasing] You just didn't know it yet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. Through the nose. Not the smog.
lines.script: [calm, steadying] Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. [dry, easy] Through the nose. Not the smog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: They're gone, but he's still out of it. Look at him.
lines.script: [low, worried] They're gone, but he's still out of it. [quiet, uneasy] Look at him.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Nobody needs to go anywhere. Nobody needs to get any older.
lines.script: [hazy, serene] Nobody needs to go anywhere. [gentle, wistful] Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's not a Mr. Washington sentence. Let's check on the boulevard. Miss Odette and Doña Carmen.
lines.script: [dry, unsettled] That's not a Mr. Washington sentence. [brisk, resolved] Let's check on the boulevard. [calm, steady] Miss Odette and Doña Carmen.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Stirring. Stirring. The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn’t that nice?
lines.script: [dreamy, lulling] Stirring. ...Stirring. The gumbo NEVER has to be done, baby. [soft, content] Isn’t that nice?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's made that gumbo every day for fifty years. It's never once been "never done."
lines.script: [dry, uneasy] She's made that gumbo every day for fifty years. [low, worried] It's never once been "never done."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The smog wants everything to stay exactly the same. Forever. That's not a nice afternoon. That's a hostage situation.
lines.script: [dry, grim] The smog wants everything to stay exactly the same. Forever. [flat, deadpan] That's not a nice afternoon. [cold, dry] That's a hostage situation.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine. It's always this afternoon. Why did I ever flip them?
lines.script: [cheerful, hollow] The pupusas are fine. EVERYTHING is fine. [dazed, small] It's always this afternoon. [lost, plaintive] Why did I ever flip them?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. That's the same purple stuff.
lines.script: [low, alert] Nara is right. [tense, wry] That's not kitchen smoke. That's the same purple stuff.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look north. It's all coming down off the hills.
lines.script: [low, urgent] Babe. Look north. [uneasy, hushed] It's all coming down off the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The Observatory. The pipes on the side are pumping it out like a smoke machine on a bad set.
lines.script: [dry, grim] The Observatory. [wry, amused] The pipes on the side are pumping it out like a smoke machine [dry, flat] on a bad set.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then that's where we're going. Nara, stay close.
lines.script: [calm, resolved] Then that's where we're going. [gentle, soft] Nara, stay close.

lines.speaker: Ticket Flurry
lines.text: Street cleaning. Tuesday. Eight to ten. You didn't read the sign. And the smog says we can stay forever.
lines.script: [officious, clipped] Street cleaning. Tuesday. Eight to ten. [smug, nasal] You didn't read the sign. [gleeful, menacing] And the smog says we can stay forever.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I take the Metro. You have nothing on me.
lines.script: [smooth, smug] I take the Metro. [dry, unbothered] You have nothing on me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.
lines.script: [easy, rallying] Up, everybody. [wry, warm] Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Contested. Appeal granted. Keep going.
lines.script: [dry, official] Contested. Appeal granted. [brisk, calm] Keep going.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Nice hike. You look like you have snacks. And the dog looks like a snack.
lines.script: [sly, leering] Nice hike. You look like you have snacks. [hungry, gloating] And the dog looks like a snack.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Pack Howl. For the fluffy one.
lines.script: [fierce, howling] Pack Howl. [snarling, eager] For the fluffy one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. Ready, babe?
lines.script: [easy, flirty] Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. [teasing, soft] Ready, babe?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Ready. Kiss accepted. The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.
lines.script: [warm, dry] Ready. Kiss accepted. [brisk, calm] The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. I've seen this movie forty-seven times.
lines.script: [low, uneasy] The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. [dry, ominous] I've seen this movie forty-seven times.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: RUMBLE. Somebody plugged my pipes. Now everything is stuck. I LIKE stuck.
lines.script: [deep, sulky] RUMBLE. Somebody plugged my pipes. [grumbling, stubborn] Now everything is stuck. I LIKE stuck.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Stuck means nothing moves. Nothing changes. Nothing ever has to say goodbye.
lines.script: [heavy, slow] Stuck means nothing moves. Nothing changes. [aching, small] Nothing ever has to say goodbye.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. That's what planes are for.
lines.script: [gentle, certain] Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. [dry, fond] That's what planes are for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Things have to move.
lines.script: [firm, calm] Things have to move.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well... looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.
lines.script: [playful, smooth] Well, well, well... [dry, punny] looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one, everybody.
lines.script: [crisp, commanding] Cut. Reset. [brisk, easy] Back to one, everybody.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. Or one of our Tombos.
lines.script: [easy, coaching] Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. [brisk, practical] When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. [wry, upbeat] Or one of our Tombos.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. You asked how I was doing. Nobody has asked in a million years.
lines.script: [deep, stunned] Rumble. You asked how I was doing. [small, wondering] Nobody has asked in a million years.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: ...I'll let things move. A little. Two inches a year. That's my best offer.
lines.script: [grudging, shy] ...I'll let things move. A little. [gruff, mumbling] Two inches a year. That's my best offer.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. Fine. The pipes are clear. I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.
lines.script: [sulky, heavy] Rumble. Fine. The pipes are clear. [muttering, sheepish] I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look. The sky is blue again. LA blue. Slightly brown, but blue.
lines.script: [relieved, easy] Look. The sky is blue again. LA blue. [deadpan, fond] Slightly brown, but blue.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody plugged those pipes on purpose. Smog doesn't do that by itself.
lines.script: [dry, uneasy] Somebody plugged those pipes on purpose. [low, suspicious] Smog doesn't do that by itself.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Spooky. I love it. I hate it. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [amused, uneasy] Spooky. I love it. I hate it. [easy, steady] Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night. Zydeco from the boulevard. Kids on every porch.
lines.script: [warm, savoring] ...smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night. [rich, nostalgic] Zydeco from the boulevard. ...Kids on EVERY porch.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Where was I? Oh. I was done. That was the whole story.
lines.script: [gentle, bemused] Where was I? ...Oh. [deadpan, content] I was done. That was the whole story.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Funny. For a while there I didn't want anything to change. Then I remembered the best parts all came from things changing.
lines.script: [thoughtful, humbled] Funny. For a while there I didn't want ANYTHING to change. [warm, resolute] Then I remembered... the best parts all came from things changing.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Keep the old windows, though.
lines.script: [dry, wry] Keep the old windows, though.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Keep the old windows. Smart man.
lines.script: [warm, approving] Keep the old windows. [dry, low] ...Smart man.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Doña Carmen says the pupusas came out perfectly crispy. Miss Odette is sending over gumbo. The whole block is cooking.
lines.script: [warm, pleased] Doña Carmen says the pupusas came out perfectly crispy. [cozy, easy] Miss Odette is sending over gumbo. [happy, bright] The whole block is cooking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Home. Both of them. Okay. Good.
lines.script: [soft, relieved] Home. Both of them. [quiet, warm] Okay. Good.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Boppy has been waiting by his window since BREAKFAST. He has his fishing hat on.
lines.script: [excited, breathless] Tah Tah! Boppy has been waiting by his window since BREAKFAST. [giggly, dramatic] He has his fishing hat on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He's never caught a fish.
lines.script: [earnest, hushed] He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. [matter-of-fact, doubtful] He's never caught a fish.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we had better go help him not catch one.
lines.script: [dry, fond] Then we had better go help him [deadpan] not catch one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Back already! Look at you. Did they feed you out there? Never mind. I'll feed you.
lines.script: [bustling, delighted] Back already! Look at you. [suspicious, fussing] Did they feed you out there? [brisk, warm] Never mind. I'll feed you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Good. Sit down. No. Don't sit down. We're going fishing.
lines.script: [flustered] Tom. Good. Sit down. No. Don't sit down. [eager] We're going fishing.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw it at Cattail Pier in 1994. Nobody believes me.
lines.script: [hushed, reverent] The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. [solemn] I saw it at Cattail Pier in 1994. [deflated, huffy] Nobody believes me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody believes him.
lines.script: [flat, fond] Nobody believes him.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, is the Whisker Perch real?
lines.script: [earnest, hushed] Boppy, is the Whisker Perch [awed, soft] real?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Real as my heartburn, kiddo.
lines.script: [solemn] Real as my heartburn, [dry, fond] kiddo.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm bringing a notebook. For science. And for proof.
lines.script: [proud, bossy] I'm bringing a notebook. [prim, firm] For science. And for proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And I'm bringing THIS. My pepper jar. Homegrown, pickled in 1989. Older than your mother.
lines.script: [proud] And I'm bringing THIS. My pepper jar. [boastful, fond] Homegrown, pickled in 1989. [dry, amused] Older than your mother.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Not one pepper for me either. Peppers give me gas.
lines.script: [firm, brisk] Not one pepper for me either. [matter-of-fact, plain] Peppers give me gas.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. EVERYTHING gives you gas.
lines.script: [flat, blunt] Deedee. [bossy, deadpan] EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Who told you that.
lines.script: [flat, dangerous] Who told you that.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. At the crisp.
lines.script: [sheepish, small] Tah Tah. At the crisp.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tata is on thin ice.
lines.script: [arch, sweet] Tah Tah is [low, ominous] on thin ice.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I have three pies in, so I'm staying put. Do NOT let him eat peppers on an empty stomach.
lines.script: [brisk, stern] I have three pies in, so I'm staying put. [firm, warning] Do NOT let him eat peppers [pointed, low] on an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I never eat peppers on an empty stomach. I eat them on a full stomach. Then it's empty.
lines.script: [dry, smug] I never eat peppers on an empty stomach. [deadpan] I eat them on a full stomach. [sly, amused] Then it's empty.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: Boppy! The usual? Ginger, peppermint, and a little honey for the stomach.
lines.script: [warm, welcoming] Boppy! The usual? [cozy, fussing] Ginger, peppermint, and a little honey for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The stomach thanks you. The stomach is still complaining. But it thanks you.
lines.script: [grateful] The stomach thanks you. The stomach is still complaining. [softer] But it thanks you.

lines.speaker: The kettle
lines.text: The kettle whistles, low and long. Oolong leans in to listen.
lines.script: [low, hushed] The kettle whistles, low and long. [secretive, hushed] Oolong leans in to listen.

lines.speaker: The kettle
lines.text: The kettle whistles, low and long. Oolong leans in to listen.
lines.script: [low, hushed] The kettle whistles, low and long. [secretive, hushed] Oolong leans in to listen.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny’s. Paying double. Never takes his hat off.
lines.script: [conspiratorial, whispering] The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny’s. [hushed, scandalized] Paying DOUBLE. [ominous, delighted] ...Never takes his hat off.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: On Long Island? Nobody here pays double for anything.
lines.script: [dry, skeptical] On Long Island? [flat, wry] Nobody here pays double for anything.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle also says it'll rain on Tuesday. The kettle is wrong a lot. Enjoy the pier.
lines.script: [breezy, merry] The kettle also says it'll rain on Tuesday. [prim, airy] The kettle is wrong... a lot. [warm, bright] Enjoy the pier.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You did. Forty times.
lines.script: [flat, patient] You did. Forty times.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then forty-one. First year of college. Cross country. Five miles through the woods, up the big hill, and I never breathed hard.
lines.script: [undeterred, proud] Then forty-one. [nostalgic, boastful] First year of college. Cross country. Five miles through the woods, up the big hill, [swaggering] and I never breathed hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Last hill, I passed the whole field. Champion. They put my name on a plaque. The plaque is in a box. Somewhere.
lines.script: [proud, boastful] Last hill, I passed the whole field. Champion. [offhand] They put my name on a plaque. [deflated, dry] The plaque is in a box. Somewhere.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can you still run that fast?
lines.script: [curious, earnest] Can you still run that fast?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Sure. Sure I can. I just choose not to. It's bad for the stomach.
lines.script: [hesitant, bluffing] ...Sure. Sure I can. [airy, defensive] I just choose not to. [dry, rueful] It's bad for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Race you to the pier, Boppy!
lines.script: [gleeful, challenging] Race you to the pier, Boppy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Last one there's a soggy sock!
lines.script: [bossy, taunting] Last one there's a soggy sock!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Why is everybody walking like they're going to a fire? Slow down! My stomach is doing flips!
lines.script: [wheezing, aghast] Why is everybody walking like they're going to a fire? [pleading] Slow down! [pained, grumbling] My stomach is doing flips!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy speed, everybody. We walk at Boppy speed.
lines.script: [dry, calm] Boppy speed, everybody. [deadpan, steady] We walk at Boppy speed.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: This is the spot. Forty years, this spot. Now everybody be QUIET.
lines.script: [reverent] This is the spot. Forty years, this spot. [mock-stern, hushed] Now everybody be QUIET.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I AM BEING QUIET.
lines.script: [loud, indignant] I AM BEING QUIET.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. Inside voice. Outside.
lines.script: [prim, exasperated] Rose. Inside voice. Outside.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Shhh. Quiet on the pier, everybody. Boppy has a whole system.
lines.script: [hushed, dry] Shhh. Quiet on the pier, everybody. [deadpan, respectful] Boppy has a whole system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom holds the tackle box. I cast. The fish comes. Nobody talks. That's the system.
lines.script: [serious] Tom holds the tackle box. I cast. The fish comes. [firm, hushed] Nobody talks. [proud] That's the system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Any minute now.
lines.script: [patient] ...Any minute now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's been a minute. I wrote it down.
lines.script: [whispering, dry] It's been a minute. [matter-of-fact, prim] I wrote it down.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Snack. A pickled pepper settles the stomach.
lines.script: [casual] Snack. [innocent, hushed] A pickled pepper settles the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee said NO peppers.
lines.script: [whispering, scandalized] Deedee said NO peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Deedee isn't here.
lines.script: [flat, smug] Deedee isn't here.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: BLORP.
lines.script: [deep, gurgling] BLORP.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! A FISH! A HUGE ONE! WITH A MUSTACHE!
lines.script: [ecstatic, shrill] TAH TAH! A FISH! [squealing, breathless] A HUGE ONE! WITH A MUSTACHE!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's no perch. That's OLD IRON-GILL. I saw him in 1994! I TOLD everybody!
lines.script: [hushed, electrified] That's no perch. That's OLD IRON-GILL. [shouting, triumphant] I saw him in 1994! [fired up, loud] I TOLD everybody!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Something smells like peppers.
lines.script: [slow, gurgling] Blorp. [dreamy, hungry] Something smells like peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: MY JAR!
lines.script: [panicked, yelping] MY JAR!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: GULP. Spicy. I love it. Bye.
lines.script: [smug, gurgling] GULP. [blissful, slow] Spicy. I love it. Bye.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Pickled in 1989. Nobody takes Boppy’s peppers. NOBODY.
lines.script: [seething] Pickled in 1989. [furious, rising] Nobody takes Boppy’s peppers. NOBODY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He went west. Into the Whispering Marsh. Come on. And nobody walk fast.
lines.script: [determined] He went west. Into the Whispering Marsh. [mock-stern, bossy] Come on. And nobody walk fast.

lines.speaker: Soggy Sock
lines.text: Squelch. Have you seen my other sock? It looks just like me. It's ALSO angry.
lines.script: [soggy, grumbling] Squelch. Have you seen my other sock? [sad, petty] It looks just like me. [sulky, aggrieved] It's ALSO angry.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, that sock has a FACE.
lines.script: [whispering, fascinated] Tah Tah, that sock has a FACE.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Marsh junk. Everything people drop out here ends up grumpy about it. Like me, at the DMV.
lines.script: [grumbling] Marsh junk. Everything people drop out here ends up grumpy about it. [dry, wry] Like me, at the DMV.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.
lines.script: [brisk] Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. [dry, weary] Again.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Socks. Out here. Nobody keeps track of their socks anymore.
lines.script: [grumbling, disapproving] Socks. Out here. [huffy, muttering] Nobody keeps track of their socks anymore.

lines.speaker: Tangle
lines.text: Snarl. Somebody cast me badly in 1997. I've been in a knot ever since. Nobody gets past ME.
lines.script: [low, gravelly] Snarl. [bitter, snappish] Somebody cast me badly in 1997. I've been in a knot ever since. [defiant, boastful] Nobody gets past ME.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Excuse me? Nobody gets past ME. That's MY line. I was saying that at Rikers before you were a knot.
lines.script: [indignant, offended] Excuse me? Nobody gets past ME. [outraged] That's MY line. [boastful] I was saying that at Rikers before you were a knot.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, you're breathing kind of hard.
lines.script: [concerned, tentative] Boppy, you're breathing kind of hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm breathing EXACTLY as hard as I want to.
lines.script: [wheezing, defensive] I'm breathing EXACTLY as hard as I want to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We take it slow. Iron-Gill’s wake goes northwest, toward those big reeds.
lines.script: [calm, gentle] We take it slow. [focused, steady] Iron-Gill’s wake goes northwest, toward those big reeds.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The old reeds. When I was a kid we said there was a sundial back in there that told the wrong time.
lines.script: [musing, nostalgic] The old reeds. [mysterious] When I was a kid we said there was a sundial back in there that told the wrong time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Sundials can't tell the wrong time. That's not how sundials work.
lines.script: [prissy, certain] Sundials can't tell the wrong time. [bossy, exasperated] That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's what I said.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] That's what I said.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. There used to be a boardwalk through here. Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.
lines.script: [hushed, atmospheric] Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. [low, steady] There used to be a boardwalk through here. [ominous, low] Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. There used to be a boardwalk through here. Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.
lines.script: [hushed, atmospheric] Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. [low, steady] There used to be a boardwalk through here. [ominous, low] Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we ask it nicely to move. Iron-Gill isn't keeping that jar.
lines.script: [dry, calm] Then we ask it nicely to move. [firm, protective] Iron-Gill isn't keeping that jar.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Creak. This was a boardwalk once. Now it's MY spot. Everything catches on me here. I like it.
lines.script: [creaky, smug] Creak. This was a boardwalk once. Now it's MY spot. [dreamy, defiant] Everything catches on me here. [contented, creaky] I like it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You're sitting on the way to Sundial Hollow. Shove over.
lines.script: [impatient] You're sitting on the way to Sundial Hollow. [brisk] Shove over.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Make me. Slowly. I'm very heavy when wet. I'm always wet.
lines.script: [slow, lazy] Make me. Slowly. [sluggish, proud] I'm very heavy when wet. I'm always wet.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a LOG with a BOOT.
lines.script: [whispering, delighted] Tah Tah, it's a LOG [giggly, hushed] with a BOOT.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. Behind it, the old reeds lean apart around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. [hushed, marveling] Behind it, the old reeds lean apart [warm, gentle] around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. Behind it, the old reeds lean apart around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. [hushed, marveling] Behind it, the old reeds lean apart [warm, gentle] around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A secret boardwalk. Of course there's a secret boardwalk.
lines.script: [delighted, dramatic] A secret boardwalk. [knowing, thrilled] Of course there's a secret boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Not secret. Just old. Like me. Nobody comes back here anymore.
lines.script: [dry] Not secret. Just old. [wry, soft] Like me. Nobody comes back here anymore.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine. It hasn't changed. It still says seven.
lines.script: [quiet, nostalgic] Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine. [wry, tender] It hasn't changed. [dry, pointed] It still says seven.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's the AFTERNOON. The sun is right there. Sundials can't be wrong. That's not how sundials work.
lines.script: [bossy, lecturing] It's the AFTERNOON. The sun is right there. [exasperated, firm] Sundials can't be wrong. [flat, prim] That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Something shiny is stuck in it!
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Tah Tah! [squealing, excited] Something shiny is stuck in it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A coin. Wedged right under the pointer. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.
lines.script: [dry, curious] A coin. Wedged right under the pointer. [low, suspicious] Somebody pushed this in on purpose.

lines.speaker: The sundial
lines.text: Click. The shadow swings all the way around the dial and settles on the right hour.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] Click. [hushed, wondering] The shadow swings all the way around the dial [warm, gentle] and settles on the right hour.

lines.speaker: The sundial
lines.text: Click. The shadow swings all the way around the dial and settles on the right hour.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] Click. [hushed, wondering] The shadow swings all the way around the dial [warm, gentle] and settles on the right hour.

lines.speaker: The spillway
lines.text: Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, then drains away to mud. The way to the Deep Pool is open.
lines.script: [hushed, unhurried] Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, [slow, wondering] then drains away to mud. [quiet, triumphant] The way to the Deep Pool is open.

lines.speaker: The spillway
lines.text: Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, then drains away to mud. The way to the Deep Pool is open.
lines.script: [hushed, unhurried] Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, [slow, wondering] then drains away to mud. [quiet, triumphant] The way to the Deep Pool is open.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It MOVED. Shadows don't move like that. I'm writing this down. In pen.
lines.script: [amazed, bossy] It MOVED. Shadows don't move like that. [emphatic, firm] I'm writing this down. In pen.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old gold. Keep that in your pocket, Tom. Penny will want to hear about it. Penny wants to hear about everything.
lines.script: [impressed] Old gold. [practical] Keep that in your pocket, Tom. [dry, amused] Penny will want to hear about it. Penny wants to hear about everything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Now. The Deep Pool. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.
lines.script: [determined] Now. The Deep Pool. [knowing] That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Deep Pool. Nobody has ever seen the bottom. My father said it goes all the way to Ohio.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] The Deep Pool. Nobody has ever seen the bottom. [dry, deadpan] My father said it goes [flat] all the way to Ohio.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. The old man. And his small, loud friends.
lines.script: [deep, sulky] Blorp. The old man. [sniffy, aggrieved] And his small, loud friends.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You took my jar.
lines.script: [flat, accusing] You took my jar.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: I took your jar. Forty years you sit on that pier and you never once come to visit. You only ever bring HOOKS.
lines.script: [wounded, gurgling] I took your jar. [aching, petulant] Forty years you sit on that pier and you never once come to visit. [bitter, snapping] You only ever bring HOOKS.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, he's sad! And spicy!
lines.script: [earnest, hushed] Boppy, he's sad! [delighted, breathless] And spicy!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He's a FISH, kiddo.
lines.script: [exasperated] He's a FISH, [flat, dry] kiddo.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Tackle box. We do this the old way.
lines.script: [fired up] Tom. Tackle box. [steady] We do this the old way.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Quiet on the pier, everybody.
lines.script: [hushed, dry] Quiet on the pier, [solemn, soft] everybody.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good.
lines.script: [brisk] Headcount. One, two, three, four. [satisfied] Good.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He belches every third turn, Tom. Heal right after. When he dives, hit the water hard, or do our Tombo.
lines.script: [tactical] He belches every third turn, Tom. [firm, brisk] Heal right after. [brisk] When he dives, hit the water hard, or do our Tombo.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Fine. FINE. Take your jar. It was too spicy anyway.
lines.script: [sulky, gurgling] Blorp. Fine. FINE. [grudging, mumbling] Take your jar. It was too spicy anyway.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My jar. Still sealed. Still hot.
lines.script: [quiet, relieved] My jar. Still sealed. [fond] Still hot.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And look at that. Forty years, and I finally caught Old Iron-Gill.
lines.script: [slow, wondering] And look at that. [proud] Forty years, and I finally caught Old Iron-Gill.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Technically he caught your jar, and then we caught him. I'm writing it down anyway. For proof.
lines.script: [bossy, precise] Technically he caught your jar, and then we caught him. [firm, brisk] I'm writing it down anyway. [smug, prim] For proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Put the date. Put the time. Use the sundial. It works now.
lines.script: [pleased] Put the date. Put the time. [proud] Use the sundial. It works now.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Go on, you old bucket. Catch and release. I'll come by. No hooks.
lines.script: [gentle] Go on, you old bucket. Catch and release. I'll come by. [soft, dry] No hooks.

lines.speaker: Deep Pool
lines.text: Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. The bubbles look almost friendly.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. [warm, quiet] The bubbles look almost friendly.

lines.speaker: Deep Pool
lines.text: Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. The bubbles look almost friendly.
lines.script: [soft, unhurried] Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. [warm, quiet] The bubbles look almost friendly.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, can we go home now? I want to tell Deedee EVERYTHING.
lines.script: [tired, happy] Boppy, can we go home now? [eager, bubbly] I want to tell Deedee EVERYTHING.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Everything except the pepper part.
lines.script: [dry, sly] Everything except [conspiratorial] the pepper part.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ESPECIALLY the pepper part.
lines.script: [gleeful, loud] ESPECIALLY the pepper part.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There they are! Well? Did anybody catch anything?
lines.script: [warm, bustling] There they are! [eager, curious] Well? Did anybody catch anything?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Dee. I TOLD everybody.
lines.script: [proud] Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Dee. [fired up, firm] I TOLD everybody.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody believed you.
lines.script: [soft, teasing] Nobody believed you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I have proof. It's in my notebook. With the time. From a sundial.
lines.script: [smug, proud] I have proof. It's in my notebook. [prim, matter-of-fact] With the time. From a sundial.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! Boppy almost ate a PEPPER! On the pier! Before LUNCH!
lines.script: [breathless, scandalized] Deedee! Boppy almost ate a PEPPER! [shrill, urgent] On the pier! Before LUNCH!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Did he.
lines.script: [slow, ominous] Did he.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hand me my glasses. I want to look at him properly. Where ARE my glasses.
lines.script: [stern, low] Hand me my glasses. [pointed, low] I want to look at him properly. [flustered, rattled] Where ARE my glasses.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Apron pocket, Deedee!
lines.script: [bright, helpful] Apron pocket, Deedee!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Thank you, Rosie. Now. Let me look at him.
lines.script: [warm, sweet] Thank you, Rosie. [low, stern] Now. Let me look at him.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Almost isn't eating. Almost is fine.
lines.script: [sheepish, mumbling] ...Almost isn't eating. [muttering, hopeful] Almost is fine.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Sit down, you. I made rhubarb crisp. Everybody sit. And eat SLOWLY.
lines.script: [bossy, loving] Sit down, you. I made rhubarb crisp. [brisk, firm] Everybody sit. And eat SLOWLY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Slowly. Finally. Somebody in this family gets it.
lines.script: [surprised, delighted] Slowly. Finally. [dry, fond] Somebody in this family gets it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Best fishing trip ever. Nobody fell in. Mostly.
lines.script: [dry, content] Best fishing trip ever. [deadpan, wry] Nobody fell in... Mostly.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I love you all to the moon and back. Now eat.
lines.script: [tender, warm] I love you all to the moon and back. [bossy, fond] Now eat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew in for my big day. I'm on a forty-minute lunch. I spent thirty of it on the Metro.
lines.script: [warm, teasing] Look who flew in for my big day. [dry, amused] I'm on a forty-minute lunch. [deadpan, delighted] I spent thirty of it on the Metro.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the train to meet the plane.
lines.script: [dry, touched] You took the train to meet the plane.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I took the train to meet the man. The plane was a bonus.
lines.script: [soft, sincere] I took the train to meet the man. [playful, easy] The plane was a bonus.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Big shoot today. BACKLOT BEDLAM. Car chases, a saloon, a fake New York. I have forty costumes on one rack, and every single one is steamed.
lines.script: [bouncy, excited] Big shoot today. [dramatic, announcing] BACKLOT BEDLAM. Car chases, a saloon, a fake New York. [proud, breathless] I have forty costumes on one rack, and every single one is steamed.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, Olivia dropped Nara at your place again. Family trip to the desert. She's been howling at your front door since nine.
lines.script: [casual, rueful] Also, Olivia dropped Nara at your place again. [easy, light] Family trip to the desert. [sympathetic, amused] She's been howling at your front door since nine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we get Nara. Then I watch you be very important. I'm not joking.
lines.script: [resolute, dry] Then we get Nara. [warm, deadpan] Then I watch you be very important. [sincere, soft] I'm not joking.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Very, very important. I have a lanyard.
lines.script: [mock grand, deadpan] Very, very important. [smug, easy] I have a lanyard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi. Hi. Yes. I know. I was gone FOREVER. It was six days.
lines.script: [cooing, gentle] Hi. Hi. Yes. I know. I was gone FOREVER. [dry, fond] It was six days.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's coming to set. I already asked. Nobody said yes, but nobody said no fast enough.
lines.script: [sly, amused] She's coming to set. I already asked. [dry, easy] Nobody said yes, but nobody said no fast enough.

lines.speaker: Ray
lines.text: Sunset Gold Studios. Closed set. Name?
lines.script: [bored, flat] Sunset Gold Studios. Closed set. [monotone, slow] ...Name?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Ray, it's me. Wardrobe. I left eighty minutes ago. You waved.
lines.script: [patient, amused] Ray, it's me. Wardrobe. [pointed, dry] I left eighty minutes ago. You waved.

lines.speaker: Ray
lines.text: I wave at everybody. That's the job. Go on in.
lines.script: [bored, deadpan] I wave at EVERYBODY. That's the job. [flat, slow] Go on in.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: TNB! TNB! The rack! Rack two! It's GONE.
lines.script: [frantic, breathless] TNB! TNB! The rack! Rack two! [wailing, panicked] It's GONE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Gone? It's a rack. It has wheels. It doesn't have ambitions.
lines.script: [calm, deadpan] Gone? It's a rack. It has wheels. [dry, amused] It doesn't have ambitions.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: It was right there in Stage 7. Then the fog machine turned itself on, and the lights went out, and things started CLAPPING.
lines.script: [spooked, rapid] It was RIGHT there in Stage 7. [rising, panicky] Then the fog machine turned itself on, and the lights went out, [appalled, hushed] and things started CLAPPING.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Dana Park. Director. First feature. Without wardrobe there's no shoot. Without a shoot there's no movie.
lines.script: [clipped, stressed] Dana Park. Director. First feature. [tight, urgent] Without wardrobe there's no shoot. [grim, flat] Without a shoot... there's no MOVIE.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: And the Backlot is full of little grumpy things. One of them ate a cue card. One of them is clapping at the horse.
lines.script: [exasperated, tired] And the Backlot is full of little grumpy things. [incredulous, flat] One of them ate a cue card. [deadpan, weary] One of them is clapping... at the horse.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Friction Sprites. On a closed set.
lines.script: [flat, dry] Friction Sprites. [deadpan, weary] On a closed set.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Forty costumes. I steamed every single one. By hand. While humming.
lines.script: [aggrieved, wounded] Babe. Forty costumes. [dramatic, proud] I steamed every single one. By hand. While humming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we go get them back. Nara, stay close. This is a professional environment.
lines.script: [resolute, calm] Then we go get them back. [firm, deadpan] Nara, stay close. This is a professional environment.

lines.speaker: Toni
lines.text: Plain roast chicken. No salt, no skin, no sauce. I keep it for the grips. They're also picky.
lines.script: [proud, matter-of-fact] Plain roast chicken. No salt, no skin, no sauce. [warm, conspiratorial] I keep it for the grips. [deadpan, dry] ...They're ALSO picky.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's never eaten anything that fast. Not even my shoe.
lines.script: [amazed, amused] She's never eaten anything that fast. [deadpan, easy] Not even my shoe.

lines.speaker: Toni
lines.text: Here. For the road. Don't tell the grips.
lines.script: [sweet, hushed] Here. For the road. [whispering, mischievous] Don't tell the grips.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The Backlot. Main Street up on the left, the Western street on the right, New York down on the left. All fake. All very expensive.
lines.script: [easy, breezy] The Backlot. Main Street up on the left, the Western street on the right, New York down on the left. [dry, wry] All fake. [deadpan, amused] All very expensive.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara. NARA. Don't...
lines.script: [low, alarmed] Nara. NARA. Don't...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's a closed set! She's not on the call sheet!
lines.script: [panicked, hushed] That's a closed set! [aghast, shrill] She's not on the call sheet!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She peed on the hydrant. That hydrant is fiberglass. That hydrant is a PROP.
lines.script: [appalled, breathless] She peed on the hydrant. That hydrant is fiberglass. [wailing, scandalized] That hydrant is a PROP.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She doesn't know that. Let her have this.
lines.script: [gentle, deadpan] She doesn't know that. [soft, fond] Let her have this.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's a costume tag. That's MY tag. WARDROBE, RACK 2, HAND WASH ONLY. I underlined it twice.
lines.script: [startled, breathless] That's a costume tag. [fierce, tight] That's MY tag. WARDROBE, RACK 2, HAND WASH ONLY. [wounded, quiet] I underlined it twice.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And it smells like fog juice. The grape kind. Only Stage 7 has a fog machine.
lines.script: [thrilled, curious] And it smells like fog juice. [pleased, quick] The grape kind. [sharp, certain] Only Stage 7 has a fog machine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good girl. Professional environment, very good girl.
lines.script: [warm, deadpan] Good girl. [dry, tender] Professional environment, very good girl.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Stage 7 is locked from the inside, though. And every set out here has a Sprite on it wrecking the shoot. The crew can't work like this.
lines.script: [grim, worried] Stage 7 is locked from the inside, though. [frustrated, brisk] And every set out here has a Sprite on it wrecking the shoot. [weary, protective] The crew can't work like this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we clear the sets. One at a time. Main Street, the Western street, New York.
lines.script: [calm, decisive] Then we clear the sets. [methodical, steady] One at a time. Main Street, the Western street, New York.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: Pinch. This is MY set. I hold up the lines. Every line. I hold up this one: GO AWAY.
lines.script: [snippy, defensive] Pinch. This is MY set. [pompous, clipped] I hold up the lines. Every line. [snarling, gruff] I hold up this one: GO AWAY.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Those are the neatest cue cards I've ever seen. Is that calligraphy?
lines.script: [admiring, soft] Those are the neatest cue cards I've ever seen. [curious, kind] Is that calligraphy?

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: ...Don't try to be nice to me. Nobody is nice to me. I'll PINCH.
lines.script: [flustered, gruff] ...Don't try to be nice to me. [bitter, lonely] Nobody is nice to me. [snapping, wavering] I'll PINCH.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one. Everybody gets a touch-up.
lines.script: [brisk, soothing] Cut. Reset. Back to one. [warm, kind] Everybody gets a touch-up.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Main Street is clear. The bank is safe. The pie is still foam.
lines.script: [satisfied, relaxed] Main Street is clear. The bank is safe. [dry, wry] The pie is still foam.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! Is that bad? That feels bad.
lines.script: [crackly, breathless] (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! [alarmed, rising] The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! [small, flat] Is that bad? ...That feels bad.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: All three sets are clear. And Stage 7 just opened. That's where the fog came from.
lines.script: [tense, quiet] All three sets are clear. [low, ominous] And Stage 7 just opened. [grim, steady] That's where the fog came from.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: SNAP! Scene one, take one! SNAP! I go first! Nothing happens until I clap! SNAP!
lines.script: [manic, barking] SNAP! Scene one, take one! [bragging, shrill] SNAP! I go first! [bossy, triumphant] Nothing happens until I clap! SNAP!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's very fast. And very loud.
lines.script: [dry, flat] It's very fast. [deadpan, weary] And very loud.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's every clapper I've ever met.
lines.script: [amused, knowing] That's every clapper I've ever met.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Western street is clear. The horse can come out of its trailer now.
lines.script: [satisfied, dry] The Western street is clear. [deadpan, gentle] The horse can come out of its trailer now.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: Bzzz. I hear everything on this set. Everything. Your knees click, Tom.
lines.script: [smug, whiny] Bzzz. I hear everything on this set. Everything. [sing-song, needling] Your knees click, Tom.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Watch the screech, babe. It shuts you right up. No skills.
lines.script: [teasing, easy] Watch the screech, babe. [dry, amused] It shuts you right up. No skills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: New York is clear. It never looked better. It's plywood.
lines.script: [proud, deadpan] New York is clear. It never looked better. [dry, flat] It's plywood.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Somebody killed the work lights. And look, the catwalk is up. You only raise a catwalk when you're hiding something up there.
lines.script: [low, suspicious] Somebody killed the work lights. [hushed, curious] And look, the catwalk is up. [knowing, quiet] You only raise a catwalk when you're hiding something up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The stage set is at the top. The rack is up there. I can smell the steamer.
lines.script: [quiet, certain] The stage set is at the top. The rack is up there. [dry, proud] I can smell the steamer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The main light rig runs the catwalk motor. If I get power back to it, the catwalk comes down.
lines.script: [focused, practical] The main light rig runs the catwalk motor. [confident, easy] If I get power back to it, the catwalk comes down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Three junction boxes. They have to come up in the right order or the dimmer pops. The rig will tell us the order.
lines.script: [crisp, explaining] Three junction boxes. [cautionary, brisk] They have to come up in the right order or the dimmer pops. [reassuring, easy] The rig will tell us the order.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Blue, amber, red. And one strip of gaffer tape. Okay, two. Okay, four.
lines.script: [muttering, focused] Blue, amber, red. And one strip of gaffer tape. [sheepish, amused] Okay, two. Okay, four.

lines.speaker: Soundstage 7
lines.text: The rig hums. The work lights bang on, one row at a time. Up the middle, the catwalk groans down into place.
lines.script: [low, building] The rig hums. [brighter, steady] The work lights bang on, one row at a time. [grand, slow] Up the middle, the catwalk groans down into place.

lines.speaker: Soundstage 7
lines.text: The rig hums. The work lights bang on, one row at a time. Up the middle, the catwalk groans down into place.
lines.script: [low, building] The rig hums. [brighter, steady] The work lights bang on, one row at a time. [grand, slow] Up the middle, the catwalk groans down into place.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You fixed a whole soundstage with tape.
lines.script: [impressed, dry] You fixed a whole soundstage with tape.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I fix everything with tape. You know this. Your kitchen drawer knows this.
lines.script: [casual, smug] I fix everything with tape. You know this. [deadpan, fond] Your kitchen drawer knows this.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My rack. MY RACK. All forty. Still steamed. Oh, I could cry.
lines.script: [overwhelmed, breathless] My rack. MY RACK. All forty. Still steamed. [choked up, giddy] Oh, I could cry.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: CUT! CUT! CUT! Who said you could walk onto my set? The blocking is WRONG.
lines.script: [bellowing, imperious] CUT! CUT! CUT! [outraged, booming] Who said you could walk onto my set? [sneering, haughty] The blocking is WRONG.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Forty years I've been on this lot. Forty years of bad takes, yelled through ME. Nobody ever gets it right.
lines.script: [bitter, grandiose] Forty years I've been on this lot. [aggrieved, booming] Forty years of bad takes, yelled through ME. [wounded, sulky] Nobody ever gets it right.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the rack.
lines.script: [flat, accusing] You took the rack.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: If there are no costumes, there's no take. If there's no take, there's no BAD take. It's perfect. It's my best work.
lines.script: [smug, scheming] If there are no costumes, there's no take. [gleeful, triumphant] If there's no take, there's no BAD take. [dreamy, self-satisfied] It's perfect. It's my best work.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. It's a megaphone in a beret. It has notes.
lines.script: [incredulous, dry] Babe. It's a megaphone in a beret. [deadpan, easy] It has notes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This is a closed set. And you're not on the call sheet.
lines.script: [cool, firm] This is a closed set. [dry, final] And you're not on the call sheet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Back to one, everybody. Touch-ups.
lines.script: [brisk, rallying] Back to one, everybody. [warm, encouraging] Touch-ups.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, when it says CUT, put WARDROBE on whoever is next. When it braces, Popcorn Jump. Or just tell it GREAT TAKE. Three times.
lines.script: [quick, coaching] Babe, when it says CUT, put WARDROBE on whoever is next. [urgent, brisk] When it braces, Popcorn Jump. [sly, emphatic] Or just tell it GREAT TAKE. Three times.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Fine. FINE. That’s a wrap. On me. I'm going back in the prop closet.
lines.script: [deflated, huffy] Fine. FINE. [sulky, melodramatic] That’s a wrap. On me. [small, sheepish] I'm going back in the prop closet.

lines.speaker: Stage set
lines.text: The megaphone hops off the rack and rolls away under the set, muttering about lighting.
lines.script: [wry, amused] The megaphone hops off the rack and rolls away under the set, [sulky, muttering] muttering about lighting.

lines.speaker: Stage set
lines.text: The megaphone hops off the rack and rolls away under the set, muttering about lighting.
lines.script: [wry, amused] The megaphone hops off the rack and rolls away under the set, [sulky, muttering] muttering about lighting.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Forty. I counted. I'm going to count again. Forty.
lines.script: [dazed, quiet] Forty. I counted. [giddy, relieved] I'm going to count again. Forty.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And look. Somebody stuck a note on the steamer. "Paid in full." With a gold coin taped to it.
lines.script: [surprised, puzzled] And look. Somebody stuck a note on the steamer. [flat, amused] "Paid in full." [delighted, bright] With a gold coin taped to it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold coin. Again. Somebody keeps leaving these around. Somebody in a long coat, if Oolong’s kettle is right.
lines.script: [musing, dry] A gold coin. Again. [suspicious, thoughtful] Somebody keeps leaving these around. [low, meaningful] Somebody in a long coat, if Oolong’s kettle is right.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Spooky. I love it. I hate it. Help me push. This thing has four wheels and four opinions.
lines.script: [spooked, delighted] Spooky. I love it. I hate it. [brisk, easy] Help me push. [wry, amused] This thing has four wheels and four opinions.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: The rack! The costumes! We can shoot! We're shooting! That's a WRAP on today, everybody!
lines.script: [elated, breathless] The rack! The costumes! [triumphant, bright] We can shoot! We're shooting! [jubilant, bellowing] That's a WRAP on today, everybody!

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: WRAP PARTY AT CRAFTY! Toni made a cake! It's shaped like a clapper! It's not clapping!
lines.script: [ecstatic, shrill] WRAP PARTY AT CRAFTY! [gushing, bright] Toni made a cake! It's shaped like a clapper! [relieved, deadpan] ...It's NOT clapping!

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: TNB, the studio wants you to have this. Gold-plated. It's the steamer from the lot’s very first wardrobe department.
lines.script: [warm, proud] TNB, the studio wants you to have this. [hushed, awed] Gold-plated. [warm, reverent] It's the steamer from the lot’s very first wardrobe department.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm going to cry. I'm not going to cry. I'm a professional. I'm crying a little.
lines.script: [overcome, wavering] I'm going to cry. I'm not going to cry. [prim, dignified] I'm a professional. [teary, small] I'm crying a little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're a professional. A crying professional. I'm so proud of you.
lines.script: [tender, dry] You're a professional. A crying professional. [sincere, soft] I'm so proud of you.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: And crew jackets. Wrap Party Jackets. Only the crew gets one. You're crew now. Even the dog.
lines.script: [bright, generous] And crew jackets. Wrap Party Jackets. Only the crew gets one. [warm, matter-of-fact] You're crew now. [deadpan, fond] ...Even the dog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You know what this whole day was? A real steam-ulating experience.
lines.script: [sly, building] You know what this whole day was? [proud, delighted] A real steam-ulating experience.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew three thousand miles for that pun.
lines.script: [deadpan, resigned] I flew three thousand miles for that pun.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Worth it?
lines.script: [soft, hopeful] Worth it?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Worth it. Every mile. But for the record? That was a CLOSED set!
lines.script: [sincere, warm] Worth it. Every mile. [mock stern, emphatic] But for the record? That was a CLOSED set!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A text from Amy. "Parent-teacher conference night is Thursday. Thirty parents. I need backup. Bring snacks. And bring the good uncle."
lines.script: [dry, flat] A text from Amy. [brisk, frazzled] "Parent-teacher conference night is Thursday. Thirty parents. I need backup. [pleading, sweet] Bring snacks. And bring the good uncle."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You're the only uncle.
lines.script: [amused, flat] You're the only uncle.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Which makes me the good one. By default. I'll take it.
lines.script: [dry, smug] Which makes me the good one. By default. [content, easy] I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TOM. Oh, thank goodness.
lines.script: [relieved, breathless] TOM. Oh, thank goodness.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Two coffees. Both mine. Here, have one. That's how much I need you tonight.
lines.script: [brisk, frazzled] Two coffees. Both mine. [quick, coaxing] Here, have one. [wry, desperate] That's how much I need you tonight.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You brought me coffee. At night. That's a cry for help.
lines.script: [dry, suspicious] You brought me coffee. At night. [deadpan] That's a cry for help.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It's conference night. Thirty parents at seven o’clock. And the school has lost its mind.
lines.script: [stressed, brisk] It's conference night. Thirty parents at seven o’clock. [aghast, tight] And the school has lost its mind.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The bells ring whenever they feel like it. Every clock says a different time. And the sign-up sheet ran off.
lines.script: [rattled, clipped] The bells ring whenever they feel like it. Every clock says a different time. [flat, weary] And the sign-up sheet ran off.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ran off? Like, RAN? On legs?
lines.script: [incredulous, dramatic] Ran off? [thrilled, rising] Like, RAN? On legs?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: On little paper legs. Mrs. Kowalski saw it. She's still upset about it.
lines.script: [grave, confiding] On little paper legs. Mrs. Kowalski saw it. [sympathetic, dry] She's still upset about it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Mom. Mom. Are we going to SCHOOL? At NIGHT? That's the best thing that ever happened.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Mom. Mom. [ecstatic, shrill] Are we going to SCHOOL? At NIGHT? [reverent, breathless] That's the best thing that ever happened.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody is coming. I have a clipboard, and I'm not afraid to use it.
lines.script: [rallying, commanding] Everybody is coming. [wry, fierce] I have a clipboard, and I'm not afraid to use it.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. Then a little one: brring?
lines.script: [loud, ominous] BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. [tiny, uncertain] Then a little one: brring?

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. Then a little one: brring?
lines.script: [loud, ominous] BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. [tiny, uncertain] Then a little one: brring?

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori! Thank goodness. And you brought the whole family.
lines.script: [relieved, harried] Mrs. Gregori! Thank goodness. [warm, grateful] And you brought the whole family.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Principal Pruitt, my brother Tom. He's very good in a crisis. He's also very calm about it, which is annoying.
lines.script: [brisk, wry] Principal Pruitt, my brother Tom. [proud, teasing] He's very good in a crisis. [dry, pointed] He's also very calm about it, which is annoying.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. I hear your bells are haunted.
lines.script: [calm, polite] Hello. [deadpan] I hear your bells are haunted.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Not haunted. Grumpy. Thirty-one years in this building. I know the difference.
lines.script: [stiff, dignified] Not haunted. ...GRUMPY. [weary, matter-of-fact] Thirty-one years in this building. I know the difference.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The bells ring at random. The clocks in the hall all say different times. And the sign-up sheet got up off the table and walked into the school.
lines.script: [weary, matter-of-fact] The bells ring at random. The clocks in the hall all say different times. [deadpan, haunted] And the sign-up sheet got up off the table... and WALKED into the school.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system. The bells run on the hallway clocks. Thirty parents are on their way, and those doors won't open.
lines.script: [urgent, precise] The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system. The bells run on the hallway clocks. [anxious, tight] Thirty parents are on their way, and those doors won't open.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Doors don't just not open. That's not how doors work.
lines.script: [skeptical, bossy] Doors don't just not open. [smug, matter-of-fact] That's not how doors work.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Set every clock in the hall to seven. Seven o’clock. Not seven-thirty. Not six-fifty-nine. Seven.
lines.script: [precise, firm] Set every clock in the hall to seven. Seven o’clock. [insistent, clipped] NOT seven-thirty. NOT six-fifty-nine. [deadpan, final] ...Seven.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. A school. At NIGHT. With MONSTERS, probably.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Tah Tah. A school. At NIGHT. [spooked, delighted] With MONSTERS, probably.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay close, everybody. This is a professional learning environment.
lines.script: [calm, protective] Stay close, everybody. [dry, deadpan] This is a professional learning environment.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.
lines.script: [quiet, wary] ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That one says four. That one says nine. That one is going BACKWARDS. I teach time, Tom. This is personal.
lines.script: [outraged, brisk] That one says four. That one says nine. [indignant, rising] That one is going BACKWARDS. [tight, seething] I teach time, Tom. This is personal.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Tata! SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!
lines.script: [squealing, thrilled] Tah Tah! Tah Tah! SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Little paper feet. With glitter. They go EVERYWHERE.
lines.script: [awed, hushed] Little paper feet. With glitter. [gleeful, big] They go EVERYWHERE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I can read the doors. Room One is ART. Room Two is MUSIC. Room Three is the GYM.
lines.script: [proud, bossy] I can read the doors. [smug, crisp] Room One is ART. Room Two is MUSIC. [hesitant, unsure] Room Three is the GYM.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The gym isn't a room. It's a gym. It has a number anyway.
lines.script: [puzzled, fussy] The gym isn't a room. [matter-of-fact, brisk] It's a gym. It has a number anyway.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The footprints go into all three. Then out again. Then east, to the Cafetorium.
