lines.script: [serious, crisp] The footprints go into all three. Then out again. [dramatic, low] Then east, to the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. That's excellent detective work. Gold stars. Both of you.
lines.script: [proud, warm] Girls. That's excellent detective work. [cheerful, brisk] Gold stars. Both of you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we clear Art, Music and the Gym. After each one, we fix its clock. Seven o’clock.
lines.script: [calm, even] Then we clear Art, Music and the Gym. [practical, steady] After each one, we fix its clock. [firm] Seven o’clock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: FOR EVERYONE, LOVE DEEDEE. That's Deedee’s handwriting! Everyone means us!
lines.script: [bright, thrilled] FOR EVERYONE, LOVE DEEDEE. [triumphant, bossy] That's Deedee’s handwriting! Everyone means us!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Rhubarb crisp! Deedee brings the teachers CRISP?
lines.script: [astonished, delighted] Rhubarb crisp! [scandalized, shrill] Deedee brings the teachers CRISP?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: She never told me that. Of course she never told me that.
lines.script: [amused, exasperated] She never told me that. [resigned, fond] Of course she never told me that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To the moon and back. And apparently to the staff room.
lines.script: [dry, fond] To the moon and back. [deadpan] And apparently to the staff room.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: DING! You're LATE! Everybody is late! I ring and I ring and nobody is ever on time!
lines.script: [shrill, accusing] DING! You're LATE! [rising, aggrieved] Everybody is late! [wailing, bitter] I ring and I ring and nobody is ever on time!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I've never been late in my life. Not once. Not even when I was born. I was early.
lines.script: [stiff, offended] I've never been late in my life. Not once. [dry, smug] Not even when I was born. [deadpan] I was early.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: ...DING. Prove it.
lines.script: [sulky, flat] ...DING. Prove it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.
lines.script: [brisk, coaching] Up! Everybody up! [energetic, firm] Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, listen. The clock outside the Art room stopped spinning.
lines.script: [hushed, alert] Tah Tah, listen. [wondering, quiet] The clock outside the Art room stopped spinning.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Squelch. I glued the piano. I glued the xylophone. I glued a recorder to a tuba. It's ART.
lines.script: [thick, gleeful] Squelch. I glued the piano. I glued the xylophone. [giddy, proud] I glued a recorder to a tuba. [defensive, grand] It's ART.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's SPARKLY. I love it. I hate it. I love it.
lines.script: [whispering, dazzled] Tah Tah, it's SPARKLY. [torn, dreamy] I love it. I hate it. I love it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can't glue a xylophone. That's not how xylophones work.
lines.script: [scandalized, bossy] You can't glue a xylophone. [stern, flat] That's not how xylophones work.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The glitter footprints stop here! And over there. And on Tata.
lines.script: [excited, bright] The glitter footprints stop here! And over there. [giggly, delighted] And on Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: BOING. Everybody against the wall. Nobody picks me first. Nobody EVER picks me first.
lines.script: [booming, bitter] BOING. Everybody against the wall. [wounded, sulky] Nobody picks me first. Nobody EVER picks me first.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh, I remember you. Fourth grade. You and me. Every Friday.
lines.script: [dawning, gleeful] Oh, I remember you. [relishing, competitive] Fourth grade. You and me. Every Friday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy was the scariest kid in dodgeball. They had to make a rule about her.
lines.script: [dry, amused] Amy was the scariest kid in dodgeball. [deadpan] They had to make a rule about her.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Gregori Rule. No throwing at teachers. It's still on the wall.
lines.script: [proud, mock formal] The Gregori Rule. No throwing at teachers. [smug, fond] It's still on the wall.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. That's why I threw so hard.
lines.script: [confiding, rueful] You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. [sheepish, competitive] That's why I threw so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. I was holding a pie.
lines.script: [dry, long-suffering] I know. [deadpan, pointed] You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. I was holding a pie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You caught the pie, though.
lines.script: [sly, teasing] You caught the pie, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I caught the pie.
lines.script: [dry, smug] I caught the pie.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.
lines.script: [bright, satisfied] BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. [hushed, peaceful] Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.
lines.script: [bright, satisfied] BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. [hushed, peaceful] Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. Parents, please wait in the hall. There's something in the Cafetorium.
lines.script: [formal, relieved] (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. [measured, careful] Parents, please wait in the hall. [deadpan, low] There's... something in the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori’s brother, please go into the Cafetorium. Thank you. ...ksssh.
lines.script: [polite, deadpan] Mrs. Gregori’s brother, please go into the Cafetorium. [brisk, formal] Thank you. ...ksssh.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The footprints go in there. The sign-up sheet is in there.
lines.script: [tense, low] The footprints go in there. [determined, firm] The sign-up sheet is in there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the something.
lines.script: [hushed, ominous] And the something.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There! The sign-up sheet! On the podium!
lines.script: [breathless, urgent] There! The sign-up sheet! [sharp, excited] On the podium!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's covered in RED.
lines.script: [hushed, unnerved] It's covered in RED.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Click. Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. Every name on this sheet is written wrong.
lines.script: [prissy, cold] Click. Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. [disdainful, clipped] Every name on this sheet is written wrong.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. Gregori has TWO Rs, and nobody ever writes them neatly.
lines.script: [nitpicky, rapid] Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. [indignant, aggrieved] Gregori has TWO Rs, [bitter, sulky] and nobody ever writes them neatly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That's the conference sign-up sheet. Thirty parents are waiting for it.
lines.script: [stern, controlled] That's the conference sign-up sheet. [pointed, firm] Thirty parents are waiting for it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: A hundred thousand wrong answers, I've marked. Every quiz. Every spelling test. Every crooked line.
lines.script: [weary, aggrieved] A hundred thousand wrong answers, I've marked. [bitter, building] Every quiz. Every spelling test. [seething, clipped] Every crooked line.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Nobody ever grades ME. Nobody ever writes NEAT next to ME. So tonight, I grade the grown-ups.
lines.script: [wounded, bitter] Nobody ever grades ME. [aching, small] Nobody ever writes NEAT next to ME. [cold, prim] So tonight, I grade the grown-ups.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the sign-up sheet to grade it.
lines.script: [calm, gentle] You took the sign-up sheet to grade it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: And the bells. And the clocks. Late is late. Points off.
lines.script: [snippy, officious] And the bells. And the clocks. [curt, final] Late is late. Points off.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a PEN. With GLASSES.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Tah Tah, it's a PEN. [delighted, giggly] With GLASSES.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I'm going to count to three, and you're going to put the sheet down. One.
lines.script: [steely, calm] I'm going to count to three, and you're going to put the sheet down. [slow, ominous] One.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's her teacher voice. I'd listen.
lines.script: [low, impressed] That's her teacher voice. [deadpan] I'd listen.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everybody. Walk it off.
lines.script: [brisk, rallying] Up. Everybody. [firm, calm] Walk it off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom, when it says SEE ME, step in front of them. Grace, Squishy anyone it circles. And somebody tell it its handwriting is nice. Three times.
lines.script: [brisk, tactical] Tom, when it says SEE ME, step in front of them. Grace, Squishy anyone it circles. [sly, coaxing] And somebody tell it its handwriting is nice. [emphatic, firm] Three times.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Click. Fine. FINE. Pencils down. I'm going back in my cup.
lines.script: [deflated, huffy] Click. Fine. FINE. [sulky, muttering] Pencils down. I'm going back in my cup.

lines.speaker: Podium
lines.text: The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.
lines.script: [dry, amused] The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, [wry, brisk] and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.

lines.speaker: Podium
lines.text: The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.
lines.script: [dry, amused] The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, [wry, brisk] and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...It's going to my desk. Of course it's going to my desk.
lines.script: [uneasy, wry] ...It's going to my desk. [resigned, deadpan] Of course it's going to my desk.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The sign-up sheet! It's a bit crumpled. And look, Tata. Something is taped to the bottom.
lines.script: [excited, bright] The sign-up sheet! It's a bit crumpled. [curious, hushed] And look, Tah Tah. Something is taped to the bottom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold coin. Again. Same little clock face.
lines.script: [quiet, wary] A gold coin. Again. [thoughtful, low] Same little clock face.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sundial. The steamer. Now the sign-up sheet. Somebody keeps leaving these where we'll find them.
lines.script: [musing, low] The sundial. The steamer. Now the sign-up sheet. [uneasy, dry] Somebody keeps leaving these where we'll find them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Whoever it is has very neat tape. Look at those corners.
lines.script: [admiring, wry] Whoever it is has very neat tape. [impressed, brisk] Look at those corners.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can we keep it? I'll keep it inside Lamby.
lines.script: [pleading, earnest] Can we keep it? [solemn, certain] I'll keep it inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We keep it. In my pocket. Not inside Lamby.
lines.script: [firm, gentle] We keep it. In my pocket. [deadpan, dry] Not inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The sheet! The bells! The clocks! Parents, come on in! Conference night is ON!
lines.script: [jubilant, booming] The sheet! The bells! The clocks! [thrilled, hearty] Parents, come on in! Conference night is ON!

lines.speaker: Conference night
lines.text: For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.
lines.script: [wry, brisk] For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. [amused, light] Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. [deadpan, warm] Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.

lines.speaker: Conference night
lines.text: For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.
lines.script: [wry, brisk] For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. [amused, light] Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. [deadpan, warm] Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori. Best conference night in thirty-one years. Not one parent cried. Well. Mr. Delgado. Happy tears.
lines.script: [glowing, formal] Mrs. Gregori. Best conference night in thirty-one years. NOT one parent cried. [deadpan, dry] Well. ...Mr. Delgado. [fond, soft] Happy tears.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: This is for you. My Golden Stopwatch. Thirty-one Field Days. It's never once stopped early.
lines.script: [solemn, touched] This is for you. My Golden Stopwatch. [reverent, proud] Thirty-one Field Days. [deadpan, hushed] It's NEVER once stopped early.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Principal Pruitt, I can't take this.
lines.script: [touched, protesting] Principal Pruitt, I can't take this.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...I'm taking it. Thank you.
lines.script: [yielding, delighted] ...I'm taking it. [warm, sincere] Thank you.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: And Field Day shirts. Staff shirts. You're all staff now. Even the small loud ones.
lines.script: [cheerful, generous] And Field Day shirts. Staff shirts. You're all staff now. [deadpan, fond] ...Even the small LOUD ones.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Thirty conferences. Zero tears. One very well-behaved pen.
lines.script: [tired, triumphant] Thirty conferences. Zero tears. [dry, satisfied] One very well-behaved pen.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh. A text. From Justin.
lines.script: [soft, surprised] Oh. A text. [warm, pleased] From Justin.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: "Heard it went great. Proud of you. Stuck at work till nine. Save me a cookie." With a little heart.
lines.script: [warm, even] "Heard it went great. Proud of you. [rueful, fond] Stuck at work till nine. Save me a cookie." [softening, tender] With a little heart.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dad used the heart! He only uses the heart on special days!
lines.script: [thrilled, breathless] Dad used the heart! [emphatic, certain] He only uses the heart on special days!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Did we save a cookie for Dad?
lines.script: [pointed, mock stern] Girls. [teasing, knowing] Did we save a cookie for Dad?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...Define save.
lines.script: [sly, innocent] ...Define save.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Tata. There's a man.
lines.script: [hushed, uneasy] Tah Tah. Tah Tah. [whispering, small] There's a man.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: By the last car. In a long coat. He's looking at us.
lines.script: [whispering, spooked] By the last car. In a long coat. [faint, uneasy] He's looking at us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Nobody there.
lines.script: [quiet, uneasy] ...Nobody there.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Probably a parent. A late one. There's always a late one.
lines.script: [breezy, quick] Probably a parent. [dry, dismissive] A late one. There's always a late one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Probably.
lines.script: [quiet, unconvinced] Probably.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A long coat. Gold coins. That's what Oolong’s kettle said, too. I'm keeping a list.
lines.script: [low, thoughtful] A long coat. Gold coins. [dry, wry] That's what Oolong’s kettle said, too. [deadpan] I'm keeping a list.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm keeping a list too. Mine has a chart.
lines.script: [bright, competitive] I'm keeping a list too. [smug, pleased] Mine has a chart.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody in the van. Tom, you too. You were the good uncle tonight. By a lot.
lines.script: [brisk, warm] Everybody in the van. Tom, you too. [sincere, affectionate] You were the good uncle tonight. [emphatic, fond] By a lot.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: By default.
lines.script: [dry, flat] By default.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: By a LOT. Take the compliment, Tom.
lines.script: [firm, teasing] By a LOT. [warm, insistent] Take the compliment, Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A text from TNB.
lines.script: [dry, calm] A text from TNB.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Babe. Come home. Your house. NOW. It's about Bready Mercury."
lines.script: [flat, urgent] "Babe. Come home. Your house. NOW. [alarmed, quiet] It's about Bready Mercury."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Also there are acorns in the flour."
lines.script: [deadpan, bewildered] "Also there are acorns in the flour."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He has a key. I gave him a key for exactly this kind of emergency.
lines.script: [tense, dry] He has a key. [sinking, worried] I gave him a key for exactly this kind of emergency.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I didn't picture acorns.
lines.script: [quiet, baffled] I didn't picture acorns.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Hi. Missed you. Don't panic. Look at the island.
lines.script: [gentle, hurried] Okay. Hi. Missed you. [careful, grave] Don't panic. Look at the island.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Where's Bready Mercury.
lines.script: [tight, hushed] ...Where's Bready Mercury.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's the thing. I came over to feed him, like you asked. The jar was gone. The window was open.
lines.script: [sheepish, rushed] That's the thing. I came over to feed him, like you asked. [grim, quiet] The jar was gone. [low, uneasy] The window was open.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And there were tiny footprints in the flour. Four toes in front, five in back. I looked it up.
lines.script: [hushed, spooked] And there were tiny footprints in the flour. [precise, careful] Four toes in front, five in back. [easy, sheepish] I looked it up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Bready Mercury is nine years old. He has flown Delta One. Twice.
lines.script: [quiet, stricken] Bready Mercury is nine years old. [dry, indignant] He has flown Delta One. Twice.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I know, babe. I've seen every horror movie ever made. This is exactly how they start.
lines.script: [sympathetic, wry] I know, babe. [deadpan] I've seen every horror movie ever made. [low, ominous] This is exactly how they start.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And this was on the windowsill. An acorn. With a tiny X carved in it.
lines.script: [low, dramatic] And this was on the windowsill. [hushed, slow] An acorn. [grave, quiet] With a tiny X carved in it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody took my starter. And left a calling card.
lines.script: [cold, quiet] Somebody took my starter. [low, bitter] And left a calling card.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Olivia texted me too. Nara hasn't slept in three days. She just stands at the window and growls at trees.
lines.script: [worried, level] Olivia texted me too. [concerned, quiet] Nara hasn't slept in three days. [hushed, eerie] She just stands at the window and growls at trees.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara is scared of the vacuum. Nara doesn't growl at trees.
lines.script: [firm, dry] Nara is scared of the vacuum. [pointed, certain] Nara doesn't growl at trees.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Exactly. Something is going on out there.
lines.script: [quiet, serious] Exactly. [low, ominous] Something is going on out there.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! Oh, thank goodness. You already have her. She hasn't slept since Sunday.
lines.script: [relieved, frazzled] Tom! Oh, thank goodness. You already have her. [weary, hurried] She hasn't slept since Sunday.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! Oh, thank goodness. Can you take her? Please? She hasn't slept since Sunday.
lines.script: [relieved, frazzled] Tom! Oh, thank goodness. [pleading, breathless] Can you take her? Please? [weary, hurried] She hasn't slept since Sunday.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: That. All night. And it's not just us. Lachlan’s toy truck is gone. Mr. Washington’s reading glasses. Marisol says every tennis ball on the block.
lines.script: [hushed, urgent] That. All night. [quick, spooked] And it's not just us. Lachlan’s toy truck is gone. Mr. Washington’s reading glasses. [exasperated, incredulous] Marisol says every tennis ball on the block.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I found my car keys in the gutter. With three peanuts. Arranged in a triangle.

lines.text: "THE MOON CLUB requests the pleasure of TOM. Tonight, at moonrise. Admit three. Adults only. Dress: your very best."
lines.script: [dry, formal] "THE MOON CLUB requests the pleasure of TOM. [slow, mysterious] Tonight, at moonrise. Admit three. Adults only. [stiff, amused] Dress: your very best."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Gold wax seal. A little clock on it.
lines.script: [quiet, wary] Gold wax seal. [low, curious] A little clock on it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ADULTS ONLY? I'm basically an adult. I have a YouTube channel. I have a SKINCARE ROUTINE.
lines.script: [scandalized, indignant] ADULTS ONLY? [dramatic, arguing] I'm basically an adult. I have a YouTube channel. [haughty, proud] I have a SKINCARE ROUTINE.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm six. Is six adults?
lines.script: [small, hopeful] I'm six. [innocent, earnest] Is six adults?

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Girls. You're staying with me. I brought cards. I cheat. You'll learn a great deal.
lines.script: [dry, grand] Girls. You're staying with me. I brought cards. [arch, relishing] ...I cheat. [serene, amused] You'll learn a GREAT deal.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Forty years I've lived in this town. Every full moon, the lights used to go on in that dome above Luna’s. Nobody I know has ever been invited. Not once.
lines.script: [wistful, marveling] Forty years I've lived in this town. [hushed, nostalgic] Every full moon, the lights used to go on in that dome above Luna’s. [emphatic, wounded] Nobody I know has ever been invited. Not once.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Admit three, Tom. You. Me. And Boppy.
lines.script: [decisive, proud] Admit three, Tom. [brisk, pointed] You. Me. And Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm not wearing a tie.
lines.script: [grumbling] I'm not wearing a tie.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You're wearing the tie.
lines.script: [firm, sweet] You're wearing the tie.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...I'm wearing the tie.
lines.script: [grumbling, defeated] ...I'm wearing the tie.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: The Moon Club. I haven't heard that name since 1971.
lines.script: [hushed, wistful] The Moon Club. [slow, dreamy] I haven't heard that name since 1971.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You went?
lines.script: [surprised, curious] You went?

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Darling, I went to everything. The last dance. A big silver ball turned all night. Then they locked the doors and nobody ever said why.
lines.script: [grand, breezy] Darling, I went to EVERYTHING. [dreamy, savoring] The last dance. A big silver ball turned all night. [low, hushed] Then they locked the doors... and nobody ever said why.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: I left a coat there. Purple velvet. I was in a hurry.
lines.script: [airy, offhand] I left a coat there. Purple velvet. [deadpan, dry] ...I was in a hurry.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And now the moon is missing. Three nights. I power walk at nine. I walked straight into the Hendersons’ hedge.
lines.script: [exasperated, indignant] And now the moon is missing. Three nights. [aggrieved, dry] I power walk at nine. [flat, wounded] I walked straight into the Hendersons’ hedge.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A missing moon, a locked club, and a little gold clock. Everybody get your shoes.
lines.script: [dry, resolute] A missing moon, a locked club, and a little gold clock. [firm, brisk] Everybody get your shoes.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: Oh! Visitors. At night. Is that... is that an INVITATION?
lines.script: [surprised, delighted] Oh! Visitors. At NIGHT. [hushed, giddy] Is that... is that an INVITATION?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Moon Club. Tonight. Admit three.
lines.script: [dry, formal] The Moon Club. Tonight. [crisp, flat] Admit three.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: Twelve years I have swept this floor. That little silver door in the back has never once opened. I thought it was a closet.
lines.script: [wistful, sheepish] TWELVE years I have swept this floor. That little silver door in the back has never once opened. [sincere, quiet] ...I thought it was a closet.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: And my telescope can't find the moon. It's not behind a cloud. It's not anywhere. It's just GONE.
lines.script: [wistful, worried] And my telescope can't find the moon. [anxious, quick] It's not behind a cloud. It's not anywhere. [stricken, rising] It's just GONE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey, show her the seal.
lines.script: [warm, coaxing] Honey, show her the seal.

lines.speaker: Little silver door
lines.text: Tom holds up the invitation. The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.
lines.script: [hushed, gentle] Tom holds up the invitation. [soft, wondering] The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.

lines.speaker: Little silver door
lines.text: Tom holds up the invitation. The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.
lines.script: [hushed, gentle] Tom holds up the invitation. [soft, wondering] The brass moon on the little door clicks, and the door swings open by itself.

lines.speaker: Luna
lines.text: ...It wasn't a closet.
lines.script: [stunned, matter-of-fact] ...It WASN't a closet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Stairs. Of course it's stairs. Nobody take them fast.
lines.script: [resigned] Stairs. Of course it's stairs. [pointed, warning] Nobody take them fast.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. Oh, Tom. It's beautiful.
lines.script: [hushed, moved] Oh. Oh, Tom. [tender, soft] It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It's FILTHY. Fifty years of dust. Somebody hand me a mop.
lines.script: [brisk, appalled] It's FILTHY. Fifty years of dust. [commanding, bustling] Somebody hand me a mop.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody is here. A party and nobody is here.
lines.script: [unimpressed] Nobody is here. [grumbling, flat] A party and nobody is here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Look at the east window. Moonlight. Just a thread of it.
lines.script: [quiet, alert] Look at the east window. [soft, wondering] Moonlight. Just a thread of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The moon isn't gone. Something up in the Dome is pulling all of its light inside. Only a little gets out.
lines.script: [thoughtful, steady] The moon isn't gone. [low, serious] Something up in the Dome is pulling all of its light inside. [grave, quiet] Only a little gets out.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody read me that plaque. My glasses are in my other purse.
lines.script: [bustling, flustered] Somebody read me that plaque. [fussing, distracted] My glasses are in my other purse.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You're wearing them, Dee.
lines.script: [dry, patient] You're wearing them, Dee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. So I am. Well then.
lines.script: [sheepish, small] Oh. So I am. [breezy, unbothered] Well then.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The plaque says MEMBERS ARE ADMITTED BY MOONLIGHT. And look, three little brass stands. Somebody took the mirrors.
lines.script: [proud, grand] The plaque says MEMBERS ARE ADMITTED BY MOONLIGHT. [suspicious, sharp] And look, three little brass stands. [indignant, huffy] Somebody took the mirrors.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A coat check, a card room, a ballroom. Three rooms. Three stands. I count three suspects.
lines.script: [methodical] A coat check, a card room, a ballroom. [measured, steady] Three rooms. Three stands. [flat, certain] I count three suspects.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Assistant Deputy Warden. Rikers. I know what a lineup looks like.
lines.script: [proud] Assistant Deputy Warden. Rikers. [dry, knowing] I know what a lineup looks like.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: Ticket? Do you have a ticket? I'm holding this coat for ticket seven. She said she'd be right back.
lines.script: [prim, anxious] Ticket? Do you have a ticket? [fretful, earnest] I'm holding this coat for ticket seven. [hopeful, small] She said she'd be right back.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: That was 1971. I haven't let go once. I'm VERY good at hanging on.
lines.script: [faint, wistful] That was 1971. I haven't let go once. [chirpy, boastful] I'm VERY good at hanging on.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Purple velvet. Tom. That's Aunt Ellie’s coat.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Purple velvet. Tom. [breathless, delighted] That's Aunt Ellie’s coat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And our mirror is hanging off your other shoulder.
lines.script: [dry, calm] And our mirror is hanging off your other shoulder.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: Nobody gets anything without a ticket.
lines.script: [defensive, prim] Nobody gets anything without a ticket.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Okay, everybody up. Deedee is a nurse. Up, up. Little sip of water. Good.
lines.script: [brisk, kind] Okay, everybody up. Deedee is a nurse. [soothing, practiced] Up, up. Little sip of water. Good.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: ...Okay. Okay. You can take it to her. Tell her I held on the whole time.
lines.script: [shaky, relieved] ...Okay. Okay. [soft, trembling] You can take it to her. [aching, proud] Tell her I held on the whole time.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: We'll tell her, honey. She'll be so pleased. She'll pretend not to be. That's how you know.
lines.script: [tender, reassuring] We'll tell her, honey. She'll be so pleased. [fond, knowing] She'll pretend not to be. [warm, wry] That's how you know.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 1 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.
lines.script: [dry, matter-of-fact] A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 1 on the back. [flat, calm] It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Three mirrors. Three stands. One little moonbeam. I didn't drive a car for forty years without learning about mirrors.
lines.script: [lecturing] Three mirrors. Three stands. One little moonbeam. [smug, proud] I didn't drive a car for forty years without learning about mirrors.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You drove into the mailbox twice, honey.
lines.script: [sweet, teasing] You drove into the mailbox twice, honey.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The mailbox moved.
lines.script: [deadpan, dignified] The mailbox moved.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: Deal me in. No. Wait. Don't deal me in. You're cheating. Everybody is cheating. The MIRROR is cheating.
lines.script: [grumpy, flip-flopping] Deal me in. No. Wait. Don't deal me in. [accusing, ranting] You're cheating. Everybody is cheating. [outraged, shrill] The MIRROR is cheating.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Gin rummy with Deedee, fifty years. I've never won a hand. Not one. I know a sore loser when I see one.
lines.script: [rueful] Gin rummy with Deedee, fifty years. [flat, resigned] I've never won a hand. Not one. [dry, wry] I know a sore loser when I see one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You ARE a sore loser, honey.
lines.script: [teasing, affectionate] You ARE a sore loser, honey.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm a sore WINNER. Who hasn't won yet.
lines.script: [indignant, sulky] I'm a sore WINNER. [muttering, dry] Who hasn't won yet.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: ...Best two out of three?
lines.script: [sulky, hopeful] ...Best two out of three?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Sunday. My house. Bring your own deck. You'll lose. I'll lose too. We can lose together.
lines.script: [warming] Sunday. My house. Bring your own deck. [dry, flat] You'll lose. I'll lose too. [kindly, amused] We can lose together.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Look at you. Making a friend.
lines.script: [delighted, proud] Look at you. [warm, fond] Making a friend.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 2 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.
lines.script: [dry, matter-of-fact] A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 2 on the back. [flat, calm] It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Oh. Oh no. People. Don't look at me. I'm just here. With the wall. And this mirror. Which I'm hiding behind.
lines.script: [panicked, whispering] Oh. Oh no. People. [frantic, small] Don't look at me. I'm just here. [mumbling, tiny] With the wall. And this mirror. Which I'm hiding behind.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, sweetheart. Nobody asked you to dance, did they?
lines.script: [soft, sympathetic] Oh, sweetheart. [gentle, motherly] Nobody asked you to dance, did they?

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Every song, 1924 to 1971. I stood right here. Nobody. Ever.
lines.script: [quiet, aching] Every song, 1924 to 1971. I stood right here. [whispering, lonely] Nobody. Ever.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we'll ask. Nicely. After you give us the mirror.
lines.script: [gentle, firm] Then we'll ask. Nicely. [dry, warm] After you give us the mirror.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: ...You were very nice about it. For a fight. Here. The mirror. It was the big one, over the bandstand, before she came.
lines.script: [shy, surprised] ...You were very nice about it. For a fight. [hesitant, soft] Here. The mirror. [wistful, confiding] It was the big one, over the bandstand, before she came.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She?
lines.script: [sharp, quiet] She?

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: The Mirrorball. Up in the Dome. She hasn't stopped spinning in three nights.
lines.script: [hushed, uneasy] The Mirrorball. Up in the Dome. [worried, small] She hasn't stopped spinning in three nights.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 3 on the back. It goes on a stand in the hall.
lines.script: [dry, matter-of-fact] A round mirror in a brass frame. It says MIRROR 3 on the back. [flat, calm] It goes on a stand in the hall.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A slow one. My stomach gets one song. One. Deedee. May I.
lines.script: [tender] A slow one. My stomach gets one song. One. [softer, gallant] Deedee. May I.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Fifty-two years, and he still asks. Every time.
lines.script: [misty, fond] Fifty-two years, and he still asks. [warm, tender] Every time.

lines.speaker: Ballroom
lines.text: They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.
lines.script: [soft, tender] They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. [gentle, amused] Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.

lines.speaker: Ballroom
lines.text: They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.
lines.script: [soft, tender] They dance across the dusty floor, slow and small and very close. [gentle, amused] Boppy doesn't mention his stomach once.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: (Tom doesn't take a picture. Tom takes four pictures.)
lines.script: [dry, quiet] (Tom doesn't take a picture. [deadpan, warm] Tom takes four pictures.)

lines.speaker: Dome doors
lines.text: The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. Click. CLUNK.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering] The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. [soft, glowing] It glows. [crisp, resonant] Click. CLUNK.

lines.speaker: Dome doors
lines.text: The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. It glows. Click. CLUNK.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering] The thread of moonlight bounces off three mirrors and lands right in the middle of the moon-shaped lock. [soft, glowing] It glows. [crisp, resonant] Click. CLUNK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. Tom, feel my arm.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. [breathless, fussing] Tom, feel my arm.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Somebody up there is playing music. Very loud music. In 1971 they called that a nuisance.
lines.script: [disapproving] Somebody up there is playing music. [dry, flat] Very loud music. [grumbling, dry] In 1971 they called that a nuisance.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Over the bandstand. It's so BRIGHT. I can't look at it. I'm looking at it.
lines.script: [dazzled, flustered] Tom. Over the bandstand. It's so BRIGHT. [helpless, torn] I can't look at it. I'm looking at it.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Guests! GUESTS! Oh, at last. Welcome to the Moon Club. Nobody has come up those stairs since 1971.
lines.script: [gasping, swooning, over-the-top posh] Guests! GUESTS! [fluttering, theatrical] Oh, at LAST. [grandly, swooping pitch] Welcome to the Moon Club. [dramatic sigh, melodramatic] Nobody has come up those stairs since 1971.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Every full moon, they danced under me. Then the last dance. The band said see you next moon. Nobody came back.
lines.script: [dreamy, trilling, grand] Every full moon, they danced under me. [dramatic wail, theatrical] Then the last dance. The band said see you next moon. [quivering, melodramatic sob] Nobody came back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: So you took the moon.
lines.script: [dry, steady] So you took the moon.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: I CAUGHT it. All of it. Every bit of moonlight, right here in me.
lines.script: [haughty, trilling, aghast] I CAUGHT it. [swooping, smug, posh] All of it. Every bit of moonlight, right here in me.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: If I'm the brightest thing in the whole sky, somebody will HAVE to come dance. And look. Somebody did.
lines.script: [grandly, swooping pitch, campy] If I'm the brightest thing in the whole sky, somebody will HAVE to come dance. [gasping, delighted] And look. [shrieking with joy, over-the-top] Somebody did.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey, there's a whole town walking into hedges down there.
lines.script: [gentle, mildly scolding] Honey, there's a whole town walking into hedges down there.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Then they can come UP. One more dance. Just one. Everybody, under me, forever.
lines.script: [sniffy, haughty, posh] Then they can come UP. [melodramatic, pleading] One more dance. Just one. [booming diva, theatrical] Everybody, under me, forever.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Forever is a lot of dancing. And everybody dances too fast.
lines.script: [dry] Forever is a lot of dancing. [grumbling] And everybody dances too fast.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Deedee, Boppy, behind me. No touching, please.
lines.script: [calm, firm] Deedee, Boppy, behind me. [dry, steady] No touching, please.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, everybody. Deedee is a nurse.
lines.script: [brisk, rallying] Up, everybody. [firm, kind] Deedee is a nurse.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since 1971. Three times.
lines.script: [urgent, hushed] Tom, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. [soft, tender] And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since 1971. [meaningful, gentle] Three times.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: ...Fine. The party is over. It was over in 1971. I just didn't want to be the one to turn off the lights.
lines.script: [enormous dramatic sigh] ...Fine. [tragic, theatrical, posh] The party is over. It was over in 1971. [quivering, melodramatic] I just didn't want to be the one to turn off the lights.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, honey. Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. I'll bring crisp.
lines.script: [tender, melting] Oh, honey. [warm, reassuring] Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. [brisk, gentle] I'll bring crisp.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. The moon. Right where it belongs.
lines.script: [soft, awed] The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. [hushed, glowing] A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. [warm, satisfied] The moon. Right where it belongs.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. The moon. Right where it belongs.
lines.script: [soft, awed] The Mirrorball turns once, slowly, and lets go. [hushed, glowing] A great round light rises out of her, up through the glass, and settles in the sky. [warm, satisfied] The moon. Right where it belongs.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: One dance. Before you go. Somebody. Please.
lines.script: [fluttering, coy, posh] One dance. Before you go. [trembling, melodramatic plea] Somebody. Please.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Dance with your mother.
lines.script: [warm, insistent] Tom. [tender, bossy] Dance with your mother.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I mostly sway.
lines.script: [dry, sheepish] I mostly sway.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then sway with your mother.
lines.script: [tender, unbothered] Then sway with your mother.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. Badly. Proudly.
lines.script: [soft, fond] Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. [amused, affectionate] Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. [wry, warm] Badly. Proudly.

lines.speaker: The Dome
lines.text: Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. Badly. Proudly.
lines.script: [soft, fond] Tom and Deedee sway under the Mirrorball, and a thousand little moons go round and round the Dome. [amused, affectionate] Boppy keeps time on the bass drum. [wry, warm] Badly. Proudly.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Here. One of my little mirrors. For the lady who said she'd come back. So you can carry a bit of the moon home.
lines.script: [gushing, swooning, posh] Here. One of my little mirrors. [trilling, grateful] For the lady who said she'd come back. [grandly, sweet] So you can carry a bit of the moon home.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Something fell out of her top. On the bandstand. Something gold.
lines.script: [alert] Something fell out of her top. On the bandstand. [curious] Something gold.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. The book from 1952. The oven from 1963. Now a mirrorball from 1971.
lines.script: [dry, steady] The sundial. The steamer. The sign-up sheet. My jar. [brisk, measured] The book from 1952. The oven from 1963. [quiet, dawning] Now a mirrorball from 1971.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody invited you up here, Tom. Not her. She can't hold a pen. She's a ball.
lines.script: [thoughtful, sharp] Somebody invited you up here, Tom. [gentle, amused] Not her. She can't hold a pen. [matter-of-fact] She's a ball.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Somebody who knew you'd come. And that you'd bring your mother.
lines.script: [warm, knowing] Somebody who knew you'd come. [tender, proud] And that you'd bring your mother.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody with a little clock. I'm adding it to the list.
lines.script: [dry, intrigued] Somebody with a little clock. [deadpan, resolute] I'm adding it to the list.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA! The MOON came back! We saw it from the window! Aunt Ellie said it was probably you.
lines.script: [bursting, thrilled] TAH TAH! The MOON came back! [breathless, excited] We saw it from the window! [smug, delighted] Aunt Ellie said it was probably you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I won at cards. I cheated. Aunt Ellie said I'm a natural.
lines.script: [proud, unbothered] I won at cards. I cheated. [glowing, earnest] Aunt Ellie said I'm a natural.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: She is. It's frightening. Well? Was there a ball?
lines.script: [dry, proud] She is. It's FRIGHTENING. [arch, curious] Well? Was there a ball?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Ellie. There was a BALL. A big silver one. She remembered you. And look what we brought home.
lines.script: [bursting, emphatic] Ellie. There was a BALL. [warm, tender] A big silver one. She remembered you. [proud, bright] And look what we brought home.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: ...My coat. Ticket seven.
lines.script: [stunned, soft] ...My coat. Ticket seven.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: I left it at the last dance. I was in a hurry. I had a date with a man who turned out to be a disappointment. The coat wasn't.
lines.script: [dry, grand] I left it at the last dance. I was in a hurry. [arch, cool] I had a date with a man who turned out to be a DISAPPOINTMENT. [dry, fond] ...The coat wasn't.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: It hasn't fit me since 1972. Keep it, Tom. Somebody in this family should wear velvet properly.
lines.script: [dry, imperious] It hasn't fit me since 1972. Keep it, Tom. [arch, withering] SOMEBODY in this family should wear velvet properly.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I wore the tie. Everybody saw. Nobody can say I didn't wear the tie.
lines.script: [dignified] I wore the tie. Everybody saw. [firm, deadpan] Nobody can say I didn't wear the tie.

lines.speaker: Deedee

lines.text: Excuse me. Who are you?
lines.script: [wary, polite] Excuse me. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Marlowe

lines.text: Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s a neighborhood.
lines.script: [dry, flat] That’s a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.
lines.script: [breezy, dismissive] That’s the problem with a neighborhood. [cold, crisp] Notes.
