lines.text: He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. He snaps his fingers.
lines.script: [ominous, deliberate] He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. [sharp, crisp] He snaps his fingers.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He took the pink off the jacaranda!
lines.script: [outraged, breathless] He took the pink off the jacaranda!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t just take the pink!
lines.script: [furious, bossy] You can’t just take the pink!

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.
lines.script: [smooth, cold] I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. [soft, oily] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [crisp, satisfied] Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.
lines.script: [smooth, cold] I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. [soft, oily] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [crisp, satisfied] Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. You don’t scare me. Colors back, please.
lines.script: [steely, unflinching] I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. [flat, firm] You don’t scare me. [commanding, brisk] Colors back, please.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.
lines.script: [airy, unbothered] I don’t put things back. I take notes. [sly, smug] Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. [dry, pleased] Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.
lines.script: [airy, unbothered] I don’t put things back. I take notes. [sly, smug] Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. [dry, pleased] Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.
lines.script: [dry, fading] He walks off into the grey, [eerie, flat] humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.
lines.script: [dry, fading] He walks off into the grey, [eerie, flat] humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s turning the whole block into a backlot. And he stopped something. Look at Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [grim, controlled] He’s turning the whole block into a backlot. [sharper, urgent] And he stopped something. Look at Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s amber. It’s warmth that got stuck. Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd.
lines.script: [calm, gentle] That’s amber. It’s warmth that got stuck. [steady, practical] Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We check on the neighbors first.
lines.script: [steady, resolute] We check on the neighbors first.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Doña Carmen turned into candy.
lines.script: [hushed, amazed] Tah Tah. Doña Carmen turned into candy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s amber. Mid-sentence.
lines.script: [quiet, solemn] She’s amber. [low, wry] Mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: She’s still pointing at the volcano.
lines.script: [whispering, amused] She’s still pointing at the volcano.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Amber is just warmth that got stuck. You don’t break it. You give it somewhere to go.
lines.script: [gentle, calm] Amber is just warmth that got stuck. [soft, certain] You don’t break it. You give it somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Warmth. We’re good at warmth. Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.
lines.script: [upbeat, rallying] Warmth. We’re good at warmth. [brisk, firm] Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The comal! The pupusas!
lines.script: [breathless, excited] The comal! The pupusas!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.
lines.script: [soft, marveling] Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. [hushed, uneasy] Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. Please wake up.
lines.script: [gentle, coaxing] Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. [tender, teasing] Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. [soft, pleading] Please wake up.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.
lines.script: [hushed, delicate] A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. [warm, relieved] Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is not optional. Tom! When did you get here? Why is everything so quiet?
lines.script: [indignant, animated] ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is NOT optional. [bright, surprised] Tom! When did you get here? [confused, hushed] Why is everything so quiet?

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Where did my pupusas go?
lines.script: [appalled, sharp] WHERE did my pupusas go?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You were amber for a little while.
lines.script: [gentle, understated] You were amber for a little while.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: I was what? I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. It was a good sentence.
lines.script: [baffled, offended] I was what? [mournful, matter-of-fact] I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. ...It was a GOOD sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A man in a grey suit did it. His name is Marlowe.
lines.script: [serious, helpful] A man in a grey suit did it. [firm, accusing] His name is Marlowe.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” I said the sign is busy because the food is good.
lines.script: [indignant, scornful] That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” [proud, matter-of-fact] I said the sign is busy because the food is GOOD.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. Feed the children first. The grown-ups will pretend they’re not hungry.
lines.script: [brisk, bossy] Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. [firm, tender] Feed the children first. [dry, knowing] The grown-ups will PRETEND they’re not hungry.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Tom! Tom! Everybody stopped! Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!
lines.script: [breathless, alarmed] Tom! Tom! Everybody STOPPED! [hushed, amazed] Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. They’re amber. The grey got in through the front door.
lines.script: [calm, grim] Okay. They’re amber. [low, tense] The grey got in through the front door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Heat is just movement. When the girls can’t sleep, we run. Nobody stays stuck when they’re moving.
lines.script: [brisk, confident] Heat is just movement. [warm, knowing] When the girls can’t sleep, we run. [bright, firm] Nobody stays stuck when they’re moving.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You mean...
lines.script: [hesitant, dreading] You mean...

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody up. Girls, with me. We’re running laps around the kitchen table.
lines.script: [brisk, commanding] Everybody up. Girls, with me. [bright, firm] We’re running laps around the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Run with us, Mommy!
lines.script: [squealing, delighted] Run with us, Mommy!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap one! Knees up, Rose!
lines.script: [loud, pumped] Lap one! [brisk, encouraging] Knees up, Rose!

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: ...and that is a FOUL! That is a foul! Who has the remote?
lines.script: [groggy, booming] ...and that is a FOUL! That is a foul! [muddled, unbothered] ...Who has the remote?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap two! Grace, don’t look at the camera!
lines.script: [breathless, bright] Lap two! [mock stern] Grace, don’t look at the camera!

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Why is there a woman running around my table? Why is it a good idea? It’s a very good idea.
lines.script: [bewildered, tired] Why is there a woman running around my table? [deadpan, thoughtful] Why is it a good idea? ...It’s a VERY good idea.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap three! Everybody on the last one!
lines.script: [breathless, triumphant] Lap three! [urgent, rallying] Everybody on the last one!

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...NO. I said no. Why is everyone in my kitchen? Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?
lines.script: [indignant, groggy] ...NO. I said no. [loud, bewildered] WHY is everyone in my kitchen? [softening, amazed] Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...Okay. That one can stay.
lines.script: [grudging, blunt] ...Okay. [warm, firm] THAT one can stay.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. Run With Us, Mommy. Amy, Grace and Rose, together.
lines.script: [dry, proud] That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. [warm, formal] Run With Us, Mommy. [quiet, moved] Amy, Grace and Rose, together.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. Every yard in this city has too many and somebody always leaves them on my step.
lines.script: [brisk, generous] Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. [flat, exasperated] Every yard in this city has too many... and somebody ALWAYS leaves them on my step.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Is it okay if I say that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?
lines.script: [earnest, polite] Is it okay if I say... [glowing, hushed] that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. We don’t even have a kitchen table. We have a counter.
lines.script: [sweet, earnest] It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. [plain, innocent] We don’t even have a kitchen table. [flat, innocent] We have a counter.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.
lines.script: [smooth, annoyed] Look at that. You put the neighbors back. [dry, clipped] Very warm. Very busy. [cold, flat] Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.
lines.script: [smooth, annoyed] Look at that. You put the neighbors back. [dry, clipped] Very warm. Very busy. [cold, flat] Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The rest of the colors too, please. All of them.
lines.script: [firm, patient] The rest of the colors too, please. [commanding, brisk] All of them.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.
lines.script: [crisp, bored] Notes. This intersection has no flow. [slick, showy] Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.
lines.script: [crisp, bored] Notes. This intersection has no flow. [slick, showy] Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.
lines.script: [bright, grand] Mr. Prime! [breezy, smug] Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.
lines.script: [bright, grand] Mr. Prime! [smug, breezy] Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every light on the block is red. Every single one.
lines.script: [low, uneasy] Every light on the block is red. [flat, dry] Every single one.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. It looks sad.
lines.script: [soft, worried] Tah Tah. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. [tender, quiet] It looks sad.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.
lines.script: [smooth, patronizing] It’s not angry. It’s stuck. [airy, cold] Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. [clipped, brisk] Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.
lines.script: [smooth, patronizing] It’s not angry. It’s stuck. [airy, cold] Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. [clipped, brisk] Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. Kindness first. Hit it if it hits back.
lines.script: [easy, thoughtful] If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. [calm, warm] Kindness first. [dry, amused] Hit it if it hits back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.
lines.script: [brisk, firm] Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. [clear, steady] If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets run over. I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.
lines.script: [calm, firm] Nobody gets run over. [low, steady] I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.
lines.script: [brisk, concerned] Everybody okay? [quick, satisfied] Good. [clear, coaching] It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.
lines.script: [exhausted, deflated] ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. [small, sheepish] I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.
lines.script: [exhausted, deflated] ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. [small, sheepish] I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.
lines.script: [kind, wry] It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. [warm, teasing] You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. It’s still warm, and it’s humming.
lines.script: [quiet, curious] The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. [soft, wondering] It’s still warm, and it’s humming.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The pink is back! The jacaranda has its pink back!
lines.script: [overjoyed, squealing] The pink is back! [shrill, thrilled] The jacaranda has its pink back!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the music is back in the window.
lines.script: [soft, relieved] And the music is back in the window.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...and that is why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? Did I fall asleep? Again?
lines.script: [slow, rumbling] ...and THAT is why you never trust a Tuesday. [bewildered, gentle] Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? [unhurried, sheepish] Did I fall asleep? ...Again?

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. Thirty years I’ve waited. Thank you.
lines.script: [solemn, amazed] I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. [slow, moved] THIRTY years I’ve waited. [deadpan, heartfelt] ...Thank you.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.
lines.script: [airy, flippant] Love it. Hate it. Love it. [breezy, grudging] Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.
lines.script: [airy, flippant] Love it. Hate it. Love it. [breezy, grudging] Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.
lines.script: [smooth, sly] I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. [silky, teasing] I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.
lines.script: [smooth, sly] I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. [silky, teasing] I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Where is my mother?
lines.script: [low, tight] Where is my mother?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. She’s been making it for hours.
lines.script: [smooth, taunting] Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. [light, casual] Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. [dry, sly] She’s been making it for hours.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. She’s been making it for hours.
lines.script: [smooth, taunting] Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. [light, casual] Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. [dry, sly] She’s been making it for hours.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tell me where.
lines.script: [cold, quiet] Tell me where.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.
lines.script: [bland, singsong] Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.
lines.script: [bland, singsong] Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He just told us something he shouldn’t have.
lines.script: [sharp, alert] He just told us something he shouldn’t have.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Long Island is under glass. So we go under the glass. Or around it.
lines.script: [calm, practical] Long Island is under glass. [easy, bright] So we go under the glass. Or around it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. We start with the cab stand.
lines.script: [focused, steady] Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. [calm, decisive] We start with the cab stand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll get them back. We always make our connection.
lines.script: [quiet, resolute] We’ll get them back. [steady, certain] We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. Tell me you know where.
lines.script: [urgent, direct] Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. [low, pleading] Tell me you know where.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Tom. Sit. Not that chair. That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.
lines.script: [brisk, bossy] Tom. Sit. NOT that chair. That chair is Sal’s. [deadpan, smug] I keep it warm for him... out of spite.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.
lines.script: [chatty, conspiratorial] Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. [mischievous, hushed] What you DON’t know is what we do between airport runs.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it crimes?
lines.script: [hushed, thrilled] Is it crimes?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Letters. Eleven years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. Nobody ever opened a bag. Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.
lines.script: [proud, hushed] Letters. ELEVEN years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. Nobody ever opened a bag. [offhand, smug] Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a HUNDRED sacks of stamps.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You’ve been running a secret mail route.
lines.script: [dry, incredulous] You’ve been running a secret mail route.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A dispatch network. We call it the Network. We never came up with a better name.
lines.script: [proud, grand] A dispatch network. We call it the Network. [flat, matter-of-fact] ...We never came up with a better name.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. She’s the only thing in town that’s moving.
lines.script: [crackly, brisk] Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. [deadpan, dry] She’s the ONLY thing in town that’s moving.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. Say hi.
lines.script: [loud, matter-of-fact] Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a DOG in my lobby. [deadpan, prompting] ...Say hi.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. She just won’t stop baking.
lines.script: [crackly, warm] Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. [gentle, reassuring] Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. [fond, exasperated] She just WON’t stop baking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. Can you get me in?
lines.script: [low, urgent] Sal. [steady, direct] Can you get me in?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. But I can dig toward you.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, weary] I’m under the dome with a shovel and a VERY worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. [resolute, warm] ...But I can dig toward you.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a hobby. It was supposed to open in 2031. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.
lines.script: [hushed, proud] The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a HOBBY. [offhand, flat] It was supposed to open in 2031. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You built a transcontinental subway. As a hobby.
lines.script: [dry, amazed] You built a transcontinental subway. [flat, deadpan] As a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We got a very good deal on a drill.
lines.script: [flat, proud] We got a VERY good deal on a drill.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. Be careful of the worm.
lines.script: [low, serious] The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. [grave, urgent] Be careful of the worm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The worm.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan] The worm.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.
lines.script: [quick, amused] The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. [matter-of-fact, fond] ...She doesn’t love it.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. Somebody has to read me the tunnel.
lines.script: [brisk, urgent] I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. [serious, firm] Somebody has to read me the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m extremely good at being in charge.
lines.script: [smug, bossy] I’m extremely good at being in charge.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m in charge of snacks.
lines.script: [proud, earnest] I’m in charge of snacks.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. If Sol says stay, you stay.
lines.script: [firm, serious] Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. [stern, loving] If Sol says stay, you stay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Copy.
lines.script: [crisp, thrilled] Copy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy.
lines.script: [solemn, earnest] Copy copy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.
lines.script: [deadpan, strained] Sol. [flat, doubtful] I am leaving my children with a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.
lines.script: [proud, reassuring] Thirty years. NEVER lost a passenger. [deadpan, casual] Found two in the trunk. ...Both were fine.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Somehow that is not comforting.
lines.script: [flat, dry] Somehow that is not comforting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be on the radio the whole way. Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.
lines.script: [calm, reassuring] We’ll be on the radio the whole way. [dry, affectionate] Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snacks are critical infrastructure.
lines.script: [grave, earnest] Snacks are critical infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. We go down.
lines.script: [steady, focused] TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. [low, resolute] We go down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have my thermos. I’m always ready for a tunnel.
lines.script: [easy, amused] I have my thermos. [calm, wry] I’m always ready for a tunnel.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. That’s you. You’re employees now.
lines.script: [brisk, matter-of-fact] Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. [offhand, proud] That’s you. ...You’re employees now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. And a tunnel.
lines.script: [hushed, amazed] EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. [low, uneasy] And a tunnel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. I’m a little bit offended.
lines.script: [wry, wounded] I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. [dry, deadpan] I’m a little bit offended.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. Say “over.”
lines.script: [crisp, bossy] Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. [firm, instructing] Say “over.”

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Over.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan] Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: At the END, Tata. You say it at the end of what you say.
lines.script: [exasperated, patient] At the END, Tah Tah. [pointed, bossy] You say it at the end of what you say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I said it at the end. It was the only thing I said.
lines.script: [dry, patient] I said it at the end. [flat] It was the only thing I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snack check! Check your pockets! I put a pretzel in your left one!
lines.script: [bright, urgent] Snack check! Check your pockets! [proud, giggly] I put a pretzel in your left one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.
lines.script: [dry, touched] ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.
lines.script: [flustered, urgent] Tom! Good. Okay. [quick, breathless] Before you go in, I have to tell you something, [rushed] and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nickel. You’re shaking.
lines.script: [gentle, concerned] Nickel. You’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For years. Paid double. Never took his hat off.
lines.script: [quick, uneasy] A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For YEARS. Paid double. [slower, guilty] ...Never took his hat off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Julian Vance.
lines.script: [low, grim] Julian Vance.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.
lines.script: [sheepish, quick] We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. [guilty, small] And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid TRIPLE.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”
lines.script: [quick, emotional] Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” [softer, wobbly] And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. They were supposed to be a retirement.
lines.script: [quiet, heavy] Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. [flat, wistful] ...They were supposed to be a retirement.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Why bring them?
lines.script: [gentle, curious] Why bring them?

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. He says. I don’t know. He’s a cab driver.
lines.script: [earnest, unsure] Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. [quick, sheepish] He says. I don’t know. [deadpan, dry] ...He’s a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re giving up your retirement.
lines.script: [quiet, moved] You’re giving up your retirement.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.
lines.script: [brave, matter-of-fact] I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the BEST drawer I ever had. [brisk, rallying] Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. [annoyed, quick] Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker... and making me RUN.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You don’t have to do this.
lines.script: [soft, kind] You don’t have to do this.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.
lines.script: [steady, sincere] Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. [warm, heartfelt] I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tracks run east. We follow the rails.
lines.script: [quiet, focused] The tracks run east. [steady] We follow the rails.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Stay together. Nobody falls behind. I’ll be counting.
lines.script: [firm, protective] Stay together. Nobody falls behind. [brisk, determined] I’ll be counting.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. But the tunnel is forty feet long. Is that normal?
lines.script: [crisp, official] Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. [puzzled, suspicious] But the tunnel is forty feet long. [pointed] Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sign says halfway. I’m choosing to believe the sign.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] The sign says halfway. [calm, stubborn] I’m choosing to believe the sign.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, did you see the stone in the doorway? It’s STANDING. I think it’s the bouncer.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] Tah Tah, did you see the stone in the doorway? [whispering, certain] It’s STANDING. [earnest, hushed] I think it’s the bouncer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. Say... over... Tata?
lines.script: [crisp, worried] Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. [uneasy, pleading] Say... over... Tah Tah?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata? I can’t hear the... Tata? Tata?
lines.script: [small, scared] Tah Tah? I can’t hear the... [panicked, rising] Tah Tah? Tah Tah?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace? Rose? The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.
lines.script: [alarmed, calling] Grace? Rose? [quiet, unsettled] The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.
lines.script: [flat, cold] THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.
lines.script: [flat, cold] THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.
lines.script: [clinical, monotone] Noise is a leak. [measured, disapproving] Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.
lines.script: [clinical, monotone] Noise is a leak. [measured, disapproving] Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Who are you?
lines.script: [sharp, unafraid] Who are you?

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.
lines.script: [polite, soothing] HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. [hushed, reverent] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [soft, final] Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.
lines.script: [polite, soothing] HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. [hushed, reverent] Mr. Vance likes it quiet. [soft, final] Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. Marlowe said it too.
lines.script: [dry, tightening] That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. [flat, pointed] Marlowe said it too.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.
lines.script: [serene, proud] Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. [pleased, smooth] We are a very good team. [gentle, firm] Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.
lines.script: [serene, proud] Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. [pleased, smooth] We are a very good team. [gentle, firm] Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re being pretty quiet right now.
lines.script: [easy, amused] We’re being pretty quiet right now.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.
lines.script: [flat, clinical] You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.
lines.script: [flat, clinical] You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I teach kids for a living. I know what a person sounds like right before they say “be quiet.” You’re in the wrong tunnel.
lines.script: [steely, unimpressed] I teach kids for a living. I know what a person sounds like right before they say “be quiet.” [firm, cold] You’re in the wrong tunnel.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. It digs toward the noise. Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.
lines.script: [cold, calm] I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. [low, menacing] It digs toward the noise. [polite, dismissive] Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. It digs toward the noise. Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.
lines.script: [cold, calm] I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. [low, menacing] It digs toward the noise. [polite, dismissive] Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He left the quiet on. Is anybody else’s ears ringing?
lines.script: [wry, dazed] He left the quiet on. [light, amused] Is anybody else’s ears ringing?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The chip makes it listen for noise. So we make a lot of it. Loudly. Together.
lines.script: [dry, plotting] The chip makes it listen for noise. So we make a lot of it. [deadpan, rallying] Loudly. [warm] Together.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve been trying to get Rose to use her indoor voice for six years. I’m glad somebody finally wants her outdoor one.
lines.script: [wry, fond] I’ve been trying to get Rose to use her indoor voice for six years. [dry, delighted] I’m glad somebody finally wants her outdoor one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A cavern. A wall of amber the size of a house. And a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] A cavern. A wall of amber the size of a house. [dry, wary] And a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is the biggest drill I have ever seen.
lines.script: [dry, astonished] That is the biggest drill I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s a Dual-Coast Drill. They went with the budget model. I can tell by the bolts.
lines.script: [easy, appraising] That’s a Dual-Coast Drill. [dry, smug] They went with the budget model. I can tell by the bolts.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s not charging. It’s digging in place. Round and round.
lines.script: [puzzled, quiet] It’s not charging. It’s digging in place. [slow, hushed] Round and round.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Its lamps are pointed at the amber. Like it wants to dig through and can’t.
lines.script: [soft, sympathetic] Its lamps are pointed at the amber. [gentle, sad] Like it wants to dig through and can’t.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s been drilling at that wall for years. Nobody told it to stop.
lines.script: [quiet, tender] It’s been drilling at that wall for years. [soft, aching] Nobody told it to stop.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hit it if it hits back. Be kind first. Amy, heal. TNB, I’m on the chip. Everybody make some noise.
lines.script: [calm, commanding] Hit it if it hits back. Be kind first. [brisk, steady] Amy, heal. TNB, I’m on the chip. [rallying, louder] Everybody make some noise.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It brings the roof down every third turn, so we heal before, not after.
lines.script: [brisk, breathless] Everybody okay? [clipped, firm] Good. It brings the roof down every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. I wasn’t going anywhere. I was just digging in.
lines.script: [winded, sheepish] ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. [small, defensive] I wasn’t going anywhere. [low, sad] I was just digging in.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. I wasn’t going anywhere. I was just digging in.
lines.script: [winded, sheepish] ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. [small, defensive] I wasn’t going anywhere. [low, sad] I was just digging in.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: I’m sorry about the roof.
lines.script: [small, mortified] I’m sorry about the roof.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: I’m sorry about the roof.
lines.script: [small, mortified] I’m sorry about the roof.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody’s mad at a drill. They’re mad at whoever put a chip in it.
lines.script: [easy, kind] It’s fine. Nobody’s mad at a drill. [cool, pointed] They’re mad at whoever put a chip in it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A little grey cube just popped out of its side. The hush chip. It’s very quiet.
lines.script: [quiet, dry] A little grey cube just popped out of its side. [wry] The hush chip. [deadpan] It’s very quiet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Not anymore.
lines.script: [dry, amused] Not anymore.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! We can hear you! Sol says the radio is back! I ate a snack for you!
lines.script: [shrill, delighted] TAH TAH! We can hear you! [breathless, excited] Sol says the radio is back! [proud, sweet] I ate a snack for you!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re loud and clear. What happened? Say over. At the END.
lines.script: [crisp, relieved] Dispatch to Tom. You’re loud and clear. [eager] What happened? [bossy, exasperated] Say over. At the END.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We took care of it. Over.
lines.script: [dry, tired] We took care of it. [flat, deliberate] Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: See? You can do it.
lines.script: [smug, pleased] See? You can do it.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Sol drove me to the second mile marker and made me run. I have never been so tired and so right.
lines.script: [breathless, triumphant] Tom! Sol drove me to the second mile marker and made me RUN. [wheezing, proud] I have never been so tired... and so RIGHT.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Mine are in this bag. Penny’s are on the other side of that wall.
lines.script: [brisk, businesslike] Eleven coins. Mine are in this bag. [quick, steady] Penny’s are on the other side of that wall.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber is clear on one side. There’s a pocket behind it. Two people are in it. One of them is waving a shovel.
lines.script: [quiet, amazed] The amber is clear on one side. There’s a pocket behind it. [wry] Two people are in it. [deadpan] One of them is waving a shovel.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: (through the glass) TOMMY! Over here! Hi! Don’t hug the amber, it’s sticky!
lines.script: [muffled, thrilled] (through the glass) TOMMY! Over here! Hi! [quick, matter-of-fact] Don’t hug the amber, it’s STICKY!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) Tom! I’m so sorry! Nickel, hold up the drawer! I’ve got mine!
lines.script: [muffled, guilty] (through the glass) Tom! I’m so sorry! [urgent, bossy] Nickel, hold up the drawer! I’ve got mine!

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. On three.
lines.script: [steady, tense] Eleven coins. Hers and mine. [low, bracing] On three.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) One. Two. Don’t think about the interest. Three.
lines.script: [muffled, tense] (through the glass) One. Two. [quick, pained] Don’t think about the interest. ...Three.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The coins glow, and then they run. Gold down the glass like honey. The amber sighs and opens. Right at the height of a door.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering] The coins glow, and then they run. Gold down the glass like honey. [soft, reverent] The amber sighs and opens. [quiet, dry] Right at the height of a door.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: It worked! Gold remembers being warm! I told you! Nobody ever believes the cab driver!
lines.script: [loud, overjoyed] It worked! Gold remembers being warm! I TOLD you! [wounded, sarcastic] Nobody EVER believes the cab driver!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Nickel.
lines.script: [soft, hushed] Nickel.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny.
lines.script: [soft, moved] Penny.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: I was saving for a boat.
lines.script: [wistful, flat] I was saving... for a BOAT.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: You don’t know how to drive a boat.
lines.script: [flat, fond] You don’t know how to DRIVE a boat.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s why it was a savings.
lines.script: [cheeky, matter-of-fact] That’s WHY it was a savings.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy. Sol and I started this tunnel in 2011 with a shovel and a very good deal on a drill. I never thought anyone would walk through it.
lines.script: [warm, wistful] Tommy. Sol and I started this tunnel in 2011 with a shovel and a VERY good deal on a drill. [quiet, touched] ...I never thought anyone would walk through it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. You’re the reason I got home.
lines.script: [quiet, sincere] Sal. [warm, simple] You’re the reason I got home.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m a cab driver. That’s the whole job.
lines.script: [modest, flat] I’m a cab driver. [low, warm] ...That’s the whole job.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Tom. I’m sorry. I sold him the coins. I took the money and I didn’t ask.
lines.script: [small, remorseful] Tom. I’m sorry. [ashamed, rushed] I sold him the coins. I took the money and I didn’t ask.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You gave back the best drawer you ever had. We’re square.
lines.script: [gentle, dry] You gave back the best drawer you ever had. [kind, settled] We’re square.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: It was a very good drawer.
lines.script: [shaky, proud] It was a VERY good drawer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Can I say something? I’ve spent a lot of time fixing mugs somebody dropped. You don’t get the mug back. You get a better mug, with a gold line where it broke.
lines.script: [shy, warm] Can I say something? [gentle, proud] I’ve spent a lot of time fixing mugs somebody dropped. [soft, sincere] You don’t get the mug back. You get a better mug, with a gold line where it broke.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s a very nice way to say it.
lines.script: [moved, soft] That’s a very nice way to say it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s called kintsugi. It’s also called Tuesday.
lines.script: [light, dry] It’s called kintsugi. [deadpan] It’s also called Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TNB. You fought like somebody who’s done it his whole life.
lines.script: [warm, impressed] TNB. You fought like somebody who’s done it his whole life.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’ve carried a lot of coffee in my life. It’s mostly timing.
lines.script: [modest, amused] I’ve carried a lot of coffee in my life. [easy, dry] It’s mostly timing.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You fix things. That’s good. Nobody fixes things anymore. They throw them out and buy a new one.
lines.script: [brisk, approving] You fix things. That’s good. [pointed, scolding] Nobody fixes things anymore. They throw them out and buy a new one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m worried about him. About Tom. He says he’s fine. He’s not very good at saying the other thing.
lines.script: [low, worried] I’m worried about him. About Tom. [quiet, aching] He says he’s fine. [soft, wry] He’s not very good at saying the other thing.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom is worried about everyone except himself. We take turns. You’re on the schedule now.
lines.script: [warm, knowing] Tom is worried about everyone except himself. [gentle, welcoming] We take turns. [fond] You’re on the schedule now.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’d like that.
lines.script: [soft, touched] I’d like that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I’m standing right here.
lines.script: [dry, sheepish] I’m standing right here.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice schedule.
lines.script: [sweet, teasing] It’s a very nice schedule.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Okay. The Sub-Rail runs the rest of the way, up under Grump Hollow. It comes out at the breach. Sol’s putting the girls on the five fifteen handcar.
lines.script: [brisk, practical] Okay. The Sub-Rail runs the rest of the way, up under Grump Hollow. [quick] It comes out at the breach. [warm, reassuring] Sol’s putting the girls on the five fifteen handcar.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We heard the whole thing. Mommy. We are coming. Do not do anything dramatic.
lines.script: [bossy, determined] We heard the whole thing. Mommy. We are coming. [flat, firm] Do not do anything dramatic.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy! Tata, I have a pretzel for Nara!
lines.script: [chirpy, thrilled] Copy copy! [sweet, proud] Tah Tah, I have a pretzel for Nara!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Grace. Rose. You stay with Sol until the handcar. I love you. I’m not being dramatic.
lines.script: [firm, loving] Grace. Rose. You stay with Sol until the handcar. [soft, heartfelt] I love you. [flustered, defensive] I’m not being dramatic.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You’re being a little dramatic.
lines.script: [dry, unimpressed] You’re being a little dramatic.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: A little.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey.
lines.script: [soft, shaky] Hey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hey.
lines.script: [quiet, warm] Hey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. I know. I missed you too. I was a small gold light and I missed you the whole time.
lines.script: [low, tender] I know. I know. [soft, husky] I missed you too. [quiet, aching] I was a small gold light and I missed you the whole time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He turns to the Censor, who is looking at the floor.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You have never delivered anything.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Here. It’s a little bit squished. It’s for Deedee. It was held for pickup, but nobody picked it up, because she’s stone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is a first-timer’s route. One pretzel. One tower. Fifty-nine floors up, and then a grandmother.
lines.script: [gentle, encouraging] It is a first-timer’s route. One pretzel. One tower. [warm, wry] Fifty-nine floors up, and then a grandmother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I do not... I have never left the Office.
lines.script: [hesitant, timid] I do not... [quiet, wondering] I have never left the Office.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I do not... I have never left the Office.
lines.script: [hesitant, timid] I do not... [quiet, wondering] I have never left the Office.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The route is not far. The job is only to put a thing in someone’s hands. You are already very good at the part where you carry it.
lines.script: [patient, kind] The route is not far. [steady, gentle] The job is only to put a thing in someone’s hands. [warm, encouraging] You are already very good at the part where you carry it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: The Censor takes the pretzel in both hands, carefully, as if it were made of glass. Then he lifts his stamp, looks at it, and brings it down on the napkin. It does not say RETURN TO SENDER. It says DELIVERED.

lines.text: In the big ledger, the clean white rectangle fills itself in, one slow letter at a time. T. O. M. The ink is the exact blue of a thermos cap.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Home. Food. Then Mom and Dad. In that order.
lines.script: [brisk, steady] Okay. Home. Food. [firm, tender] Then Mom and Dad. In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: In that order.
lines.script: [dry, warm] In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stone does not respond to talking. I have checked. Stone responds to being warm for a long time with people nearby.
lines.script: [calm, dry] Stone does not respond to talking. [deadpan, mild] I have checked. [quiet, hopeful] Stone responds to being warm for a long time with people nearby.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom’s rule: a house is warm when somebody is cooking in it.
lines.script: [soft, fond] Mom’s rule: [warm, aching] a house is warm when somebody is cooking in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So we cook.
lines.script: [bright, decisive] So we cook.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A lot. We cook a LOT.
lines.script: [fierce, earnest] A lot. [beaming, emphatic] We cook a LOT.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! You’re BACK. I saw the light on at four a.m. and I thought, he’s home, and then I thought, no, that’s a different kind of light. I made a lasagna.
lines.script: [bubbly, rapid] Tom! You’re BACK. [breathless, rambling] I saw the light on at four a.m. and I thought, he’s home, and then I thought, no, that’s a different kind of light. [proud, cheerful] I made a lasagna.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. Isla ate a different rock. We are keeping a close eye on it.
lines.script: [calm, deadpan] I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. [flat, dry] Isla ate a different rock. [tired, wry] We are keeping a close eye on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I will put the rock on the mantel.
lines.script: [warm, touched] Thank you. All of you. [deadpan, sincere] I will put the rock on the mantel.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.
lines.script: [warm, bustling] I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. [proud, deadpan] And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are VERY hot. [knowing, matter-of-fact] A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” in a voice.
lines.script: [wry, knowing] Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” [pinched, strained] in a voice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. It smells like a Sunday.
lines.script: [warm, fond] The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. [soft, content] It smells like a Sunday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. You could say I handled it.
lines.script: [easy, pleased] The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. [smooth, smug] You could say I handled it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Please stop.
lines.script: [flat, pained] Please stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. I have a timer on everything. Nobody is allowed to be late for this.
lines.script: [brisk, intense] Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. [firm, competitive] I have a timer on everything. [stern, warning] Nobody is allowed to be late for this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I choreographed the pasta. It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.
lines.script: [proud, dramatic] I choreographed the pasta. [grand, serious] It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. It’s for quality.
lines.script: [solemn, earnest] I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. [dignified, prim] It’s for quality.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pasta does not go in an arc.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] The pasta does not go in an arc.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tata.
lines.script: [sweet, smug] It goes in an arc if you believe in it, [sing-song, unshakable] Tah Tah.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. He doesn’t say anything for a second.
lines.script: [soft, moved] He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, [warm, amused] and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. [quiet, full] He doesn’t say anything for a second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. We are going to the Glass Tower, and we are bringing dinner.
lines.script: [warm, resolute] Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. [firm, dry] We are going to the Glass Tower, [quiet, determined] and we are bringing dinner.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even charging. I am scared of that tower and I am going anyway.
lines.script: [booming, warm] Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. [proud, generous] Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even CHARGING. [shaky, resolved] I am scared of that tower... and I am going anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. The amber light is crawling on their hands. It is slower than before.
lines.script: [hushed, tender] The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. [soft, worried] The amber light is crawling on their hands. [quiet, uneasy] It is slower than before.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We brought dinner.
lines.script: [soft, thick] Mom. Dad. [warm, hopeful] We brought dinner.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel. It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.
lines.script: [proud, small] I brought a pretzel. [beaming, serious] It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Everybody sit. Around the plinth. Nobody leave. Plates on laps.
lines.script: [warm, easy] Everybody sit. Around the plinth. [soft, firm] Nobody leave. Plates on laps.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.
lines.script: [hushed, wondering] Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. [awed, soft] A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, [rising, breathless] then two, then nine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s working. It’s working!
lines.script: [breathless, thrilled] It’s working. It’s working!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Oh. Oh, my back. My back is going to be talking about this for a week.
lines.script: [groggy, creaky] Oh. Oh, my back. [rueful] My back is going to be talking about this for a week.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who has been in my kitchen?
lines.script: [groggy, bewildered] Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? [indignant, fussing] Who has been in my kitchen?

lines.text: DEEDEE! BOPPY!

lines.speaker: Deedee

lines.text: You get a door too.
lines.script: [warm, certain] You get a door too.

lines.text: One skill each. Whatever you are best at, that is your door.
lines.script: [calm, thoughtful] One skill each. [warm, encouraging] Whatever you are best at, that is your door.

lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was written out of the schedule. I am a very stubborn calendar entry.
lines.script: [dry, unbowed] I was written out of the schedule. [deadpan] I am a very stubborn calendar entry.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.
lines.script: [haunted, hollow] Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. [quiet, desperate] So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. [pleading, cracking] Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.

lines.text: I kept them safe.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I kept them safe.

lines.text: There are four things that will keep you out. Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. Four things I could never get past. You will not, either.

lines.script: [wry, unimpressed] Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. [dry, brisk] That is just a regular Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Four barriers. We have a plan for every one of them. Everybody ready?

lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It is a long fight, and we are a long family. We can do this again.

lines.text: The Leviathan comes apart. It does not die. It comes apart like a watch being taken out of its case, one gear at a time, every one of them still ticking.
