lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: PFFF. Thank you. I could see my own eyebrows in there.
lines.script: [breathless, relieved] PFFF. Thank you. [shaky, flat] I could see my own EYEBROWS in there.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: It was BRAIN FREEZE. A walking chest freezer. He said birthdays are a scam and nobody came to his.
lines.script: [dramatic, appalled] It was BRAIN FREEZE. A walking chest freezer. [mimicking, indignant] He said birthdays are a SCAM and nobody came to his.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: He took every scoop and ran. Three bags. One to the fountain, one up the Hollow trail, one to the pond.
lines.script: [agitated, quick] He took every scoop and ran. Three bags. [brisk, emphatic] One to the fountain, one up the Hollow trail, one to the pond.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He took MY scoops? On MY birthday?
lines.script: [outraged, incredulous] He took MY scoops? [indignant, shrill] On MY birthday?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Stealing on a BIRTHDAY? Rude.
lines.script: [disgusted, prim] Stealing on a BIRTHDAY? [scoffing, flat] Rude.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A bad guy! On a Saturday!
lines.script: [gleeful, thrilled] A bad guy! [delighted, bright] On a Saturday!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We get the scoops, we get the sundae, we're home by four.
lines.script: [calm, resolute] We get the scoops, we get the sundae, [dry, reassuring] we're home by four.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: THERE. Under the slug. Vanilla, strawberry AND mint. I can see them.
lines.script: [triumphant, urgent] THERE. Under the slug. [thrilled, quick] Vanilla, strawberry AND mint. I can see them.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Shh. Shhhh. Everybody shh. The duck and I have a plan.
lines.script: [whispering, conspiratorial] Shh. Shhhh. Everybody shh. [serious, hushed] The duck and I have a plan.

lines.speaker: Slushie Slug
lines.text: GLORP. What? WHO? Oh no. I dropped a scoop. I dropped TWO scoops.
lines.script: [startled, gurgling] GLORP. What? WHO? [dismayed, wobbly] Oh no. I dropped a scoop. I dropped TWO scoops.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up, up. It's a slug. We're not losing to a SLUG on my birthday.
lines.script: [fierce, bossy] Up, up. It's a slug. [indignant, declaring] We're not losing to a SLUG on my birthday.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the present a BIGGER puppy?
lines.script: [hopeful, innocent] Is the present a BIGGER puppy?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's not a bigger puppy.
lines.script: [deadpan, resigned] It's not a bigger puppy.

lines.speaker: Cone Head
lines.text: Halt. We hold the scoops. Chocolate. Cookie dough. Coffee.
lines.script: [stern, gravelly] Halt. We hold the scoops. [proud, reciting] Chocolate. Cookie dough. Coffee.

lines.speaker: Cone Head B
lines.text: And now we hold the cow.
lines.script: [smug, gloating] And now we hold the cow.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOO-RIELLE! Give her BACK!
lines.script: [aghast, shrieking] MOO-RIELLE! [demanding, fierce] Give her BACK!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Hi guys. Welcome back to my channel. Today a CONE stole my COW.
lines.script: [bright, chipper] Hi guys. Welcome back to my channel. [dramatic, incredulous] Today a CONE stole my COW.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Nobody filmed MY birthday.
lines.script: [flat, wounded] ...Nobody filmed MY birthday.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. The trees are TALKING.
lines.script: [hushed, spooked] Tah Tah. The trees are TALKING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The trees aren't talking. The freezer is. Eyes on the cones.
lines.script: [calm, dry] The trees aren't talking. The freezer is. [low, focused] Eyes on the cones.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up. UP. Moo-rielle needs us.
lines.script: [urgent, determined] Up. UP. [fierce, protective] Moo-rielle needs us.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Moo-rielle! You smell like mint. We'll talk about it later.
lines.script: [relieved, suspicious] Moo-rielle! You smell like mint. [airy, ominous] We'll talk about it later.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: Grrrumble. Something moved into my pond. It's COLD. I'm a POND grump, not an ICE grump.
lines.script: [low, gravelly] Grrrumble. Something moved into my pond. [sputtering, offended] It's COLD. [indignant, gruff] I'm a POND grump, not an ICE grump.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dice says nine. Nine scoops. Nine candles. Let’s go.
lines.script: [focused, bright] Dice says nine. Nine scoops. Nine candles. [determined, firm] Let’s go.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nine scoops. Nine candles. Nine years. All of it MELTS.
lines.script: [flat, cold] Nine scoops. Nine candles. Nine years. [heavy, bitter] All of it MELTS.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Not in here. Nothing melts in here. Nothing changes.
lines.script: [low, hollow] Not in here. Nothing melts in here. [cold, clinging] Nothing changes.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody came to MY birthday. So nobody gets one.
lines.script: [sulky, aching] Nobody came to MY birthday. [flat, final] So nobody gets one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We get the scoops, we get the sundae, we're home by four. Everybody ready?
lines.script: [calm, steady] We get the scoops, we get the sundae, we're home by four. [warm, even] Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, nothing WORKS.
lines.script: [frustrated, panicked] Tah Tah, nothing WORKS.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves.
lines.script: [slow, satisfied] Good. [heavy, cold] Nothing changes. Nobody leaves.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: The scoops stay. The cow stays. The small loud one stays.
lines.script: [flat, rumbling] The scoops stay. The cow stays. [cold, dismissive] The small loud one stays.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOO-RIELLE!
lines.script: [desperate, shrieking] MOO-RIELLE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace. Grab Rose. The other end. Lift with your legs.
lines.script: [urgent, calm] Grace. Grab Rose. The other end. [steady, strained] Lift with your legs.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We're leaving. We're coming back. That's a promise, not a rule.
lines.script: [low, firm] We're leaving. We're coming back. [warm, solemn] That's a promise, not a rule.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody comes back. Nobody ever comes back.
lines.script: [cold, bleak] Nobody comes back. [dull, wounded] Nobody ever comes back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. She's SLIDING.
lines.script: [alarmed, hushed] Tah Tah. She's SLIDING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She's frozen, not broken. Keep walking. Don't tip her.
lines.script: [calm, low] She's frozen, not broken. [steady, coaching] Keep walking. Don't tip her.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He took the scoops. He took Moo-rielle. He FROZE my SISTER. On my BIRTHDAY.
lines.script: [furious, trembling] He took the scoops. He took Moo-rielle. [quavering, outraged] He FROZE my SISTER. [cracking, tearful] On my BIRTHDAY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. First things first. Rose. Deedee. Warm.
lines.script: [quiet, kind] I know. [practical, firm] First things first. Rose. Deedee. Warm.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up, up. It's my birthday. Nobody stays down.
lines.script: [resolute, small] Up, up. It's my birthday. [fierce, determined] Nobody stays down.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There's my Tom! And my girls! And my... oh. OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.
lines.script: [delighted, warm] There's my Tom! And my girls! [trailing, puzzled] And my... oh. [alarmed, bewildered] OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A freezer did it. Long story. Short version: freezer.
lines.script: [dry, tired] A freezer did it. Long story. [flat, deadpan] Short version: freezer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He stole the scoops AND Moo-rielle AND he froze Rose. On my BIRTHDAY, Deedee.
lines.script: [indignant, tattling] He stole the scoops AND Moo-rielle AND he froze Rose. [dramatic, outraged] On my BIRTHDAY, Deedee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: On her BIRTHDAY. Boppy, did you hear that?
lines.script: [scandalized, fierce] On her BIRTHDAY. [calling, bossy] Boppy, did you hear that?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I heard. I'm sitting. The knee.
lines.script: [flat] I heard. [pained, dry] I'm sitting. The knee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hold on, honey. Let me read the cake box first. It has to say dairy free. Where are my glasses.
lines.script: [flustered, fussing] Hold on, honey. Let me read the cake box first. [firm, brisk] It has to say dairy free. [frazzled, distracted] Where are my glasses.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I had them. I had them a MINUTE ago.
lines.script: [frantic, fussing] I had them. [indignant, flustered] I had them a MINUTE ago.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: They're in the oven mitt, Dee. You're wearing them. On your hand.
lines.script: [dry, patient] They're in the oven mitt, Dee. [flat, amused] You're wearing them. On your hand.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: ...So they are. Don't say anything.
lines.script: [sheepish, caught] ...So they are. [low, warning] Don't say anything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I didn't. I said it to Tom.
lines.script: [innocent, dry] I didn't. [deadpan] I said it to Tom.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Dairy free. Good. Now. Rose. Come here, sweetheart. Deedee's got you.
lines.script: [satisfied, brisk] Dairy free. Good. [tender, warm] Now. Rose. Come here, sweetheart. Deedee's got you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was in the MIDDLE of a boo.
lines.script: [groggy, indignant] I was in the MIDDLE of a boo.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and back, Rosie. The MOON. And BACK.
lines.script: [overflowing, tender] To the moon and back, Rosie. [warm, emphatic] The MOON. And BACK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Cold doesn't beat cold, Tom. Warm beats cold. Always has. Ask any nurse.
lines.script: [firm, knowing] Cold doesn't beat cold, Tom. Warm beats cold. Always has. [brisk, warm] Ask any nurse.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Warm beats cold. Okay. What do we have that's warm.
lines.script: [dry, musing] Warm beats cold. Okay. [quick, practical] What do we have that's warm.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My peppers. Out back, in the garden. The hose flinched.
lines.script: [grudging] My peppers. Out back, in the garden. [dry, deadpan] The hose flinched.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Don't take the ghost one. The ghost one is MINE.
lines.script: [sharp, warning] Don't take the ghost one. [firm] The ghost one is MINE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Which one is the ghost one?
lines.script: [curious, practical] Which one is the ghost one?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The one that's looking at you.
lines.script: [ominous] The one that's looking at you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy's peppers. Red, redder, and one that's looking at me.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Boppy's peppers. Red, redder, [wary, uneasy] and one that's looking at me.

lines.speaker: Sprinkle Gremlin
lines.text: Brr! HOT! Ours! He said take every warm thing in town!
lines.script: [shrill, greedy] Brr! HOT! Ours! [whiny, urgent] He said take every warm thing in town!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He sent gremlins to the GARDEN? Tata, this freezer is organized.
lines.script: [stunned, indignant] He sent gremlins to the GARDEN? [dry, exasperated] Tah Tah, this freezer is organized.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boo. I'm practicing.
lines.script: [whispering, earnest] Boo. I'm practicing.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up. Gremlins. We're not losing to GREMLINS on my birthday.
lines.script: [fierce, bossy] Up. Gremlins. [declaring, firm] We're not losing to GREMLINS on my birthday.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: (from the window) That's enough peppers! Leave the ghost one!
lines.script: [hollering] (from the window) That's enough peppers! [firm, warning] Leave the ghost one!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I took a little one. For later. For boos.
lines.script: [sheepish, small] I took a little one. [earnest, hushed] For later. For boos.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose, give me the... fine. Keep it. Don't lick it.
lines.script: [dry, resigned] Rose, give me the... fine. [firm, flat] Keep it. Don't lick it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Three peppers. Warm things, check. Now who knows how a FREEZER works?
lines.script: [brisk, bossy] Three peppers. Warm things, check. [pondering, bright] Now who knows how a FREEZER works?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio. He owns a creamery. He's basically a freezer scientist.
lines.script: [dry, struck] Mr. Pistachio. [deadpan, sure] He owns a creamery. He's basically a freezer scientist.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: You're back! Did you... oh. No scoops. And the little one looks defrosted.
lines.script: [cheerful, hopeful] You're back! Did you... oh. [deflated, flat] No scoops. And the little one looks... defrosted.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was in an ice cube. It was boring.
lines.script: [flat, unimpressed] I was in an ice cube. [bored, plain] It was boring.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio. Brain Freeze. He came out of YOUR shop. Tell us everything.
lines.script: [serious, steady] Mr. Pistachio. Brain Freeze. He came out of YOUR shop. [gently pressing] Tell us everything.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: ...He was mine. My first chest freezer. Twenty years in the back room. Hum, hum, hum.
lines.script: [quiet, rueful] ...He was mine. My first chest freezer. [soft, nostalgic] Twenty years in the back room. [low, fond] Hum, hum, hum.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Every birthday cake in this town sat in him first. Every one. And nobody ever says thank you to a freezer.
lines.script: [wistful, tender] Every birthday cake in this town sat in him first. [earnest] Every one. [sad, rueful] And nobody ever says thank you to a freezer.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: I replaced him in the spring. Newer. Quieter. I unplugged him on a Tuesday and I didn't even say goodbye.
lines.script: [guilty, subdued] I replaced him in the spring. Newer. Quieter. [heavy, ashamed] I unplugged him on a Tuesday... [quiet, hollow] and I didn't even say goodbye.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So nobody came to his birthday because... he never HAD one.
lines.script: [slow, dawning] So nobody came to his birthday because... [quiet, softened] he never HAD one.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: He kept everybody else's. He never got his own.
lines.script: [quiet, heavy] He kept everybody else's. [aching, soft] He never got his own.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Here's the thing about a freezer, Tom. The outside is the soft part. The door. People stick things on it. Photos. Drawings. Report cards.
lines.script: [gentle, warm] Here's the thing about a freezer, Tom. The outside is the soft part. The door. [fond, unhurried] People stick things on it. [tender] Photos. Drawings. Report cards.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: In twenty years, nobody stuck one thing on him. Not one.
lines.script: [hushed, sorrowful] In twenty years, nobody stuck one thing on him. [whispering, hollow] Not one.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Is the present a puppy?
lines.script: [hopeful, scheming] Tah Tah. [earnest, sweet] Is the present a puppy?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...After cake.
lines.script: [dry, flustered] ...After cake.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you looked at your BAG.
lines.script: [accusing, triumphant] Tah Tah, you looked at your BAG.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I looked at the floor. The floor is near the bag.
lines.script: [deadpan, innocent] I looked at the floor. [flat, unruffled] The floor is near the bag.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Take these. Hot cocoa. My recipe. If you're going back up there, you'll want something warm in you.
lines.script: [warm, brisk] Take these. Hot cocoa. My recipe. [kind, practical] If you're going back up there, you'll want something warm in you.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: And Tom. If you get his door open, tell him I said happy birthday. Twenty years late.
lines.script: [warm, heartfelt] And Tom. [thick, earnest] If you get his door open, tell him I said happy birthday. [soft, rueful] Twenty years late.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There they are. No scoops. One defrosted child. Tom, status report. Ten words or less.
lines.script: [brisk, crisp] There they are. No scoops. One defrosted child. [firm, demanding] Tom, status report. Ten words or less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Freezer. Sad. Never had a birthday. Stole everything. We're going back.
lines.script: [clipped, deadpan] Freezer. Sad. Never had a birthday. Stole everything. [steady, firm] We're going back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nine words. Good.
lines.script: [approving, dry] Nine words. Good.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Listen to me. I've run thirty marathons and taught four hundred kids. You don't out-freeze a freezer.
lines.script: [firm, intense] Okay. Listen to me. [proud, brisk] I've run thirty marathons and taught four hundred kids. [sharp, certain] You don't out-freeze a freezer.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You bring the party TO him. Warm things. Loud things. The works.
lines.script: [brisk, rallying] You bring the party TO him. [punchy, firm] Warm things. Loud things. The works.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dad, why does a BANNER have copper?
lines.script: [puzzled, suspicious] Dad, why does a BANNER have copper?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Freezers have doors. Doors take magnets. Hang it ON him.
lines.script: [brisk, inspired] Freezers have doors. Doors take magnets. [commanding, certain] Hang it ON him.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ON him?
lines.script: [puzzled, small] ON him?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ON him. And Rose, baby, you Boo him so hard he forgets his own name.
lines.script: [firm, emphatic] ON him. [warm, coaxing] And Rose, baby, you Boo him so hard he forgets his own name.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a pepper for it.
lines.script: [proud, earnest] I have a pepper for it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...We'll talk about the pepper later.
lines.script: [dry, trailing] ...We'll talk about the pepper later.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Pip, Moss and Dot are coming at four. Deedee's cake is done. All you need is nine scoops and one freezer.
lines.script: [brisk, crisp] Pip, Moss and Dot are coming at four. Deedee's cake is done. [encouraging, firm] All you need is nine scoops and one freezer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And Moo-rielle.
lines.script: [quiet, determined] And Moo-rielle.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: And Moo-rielle. Go. Love you. Don't tip your sister.
lines.script: [warm, proud] And Moo-rielle. Go. Love you. [brisk, teasing] Don't tip your sister.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Up, up. It's still my birthday. We go AGAIN.
lines.script: [fierce, worn] Up, up. It's still my birthday. [determined, rallying] We go AGAIN.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...You came back.
lines.script: [startled, flat] ...You came back.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Nobody comes back.
lines.script: [hollow, bitter] Nobody comes back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's STILL my birthday. And you have my COW.
lines.script: [defiant, bossy] It's STILL my birthday. [furious, shrill] And you have my COW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a pepper in my pocket and I'm not afraid to use it.
lines.script: [grim, hushed] I have a pepper in my pocket... [fierce, serious] and I'm not afraid to use it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody's afraid of the pepper, Rose. Everybody ready? Warm things out.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Nobody's afraid of the pepper, Rose. [steady, calm] Everybody ready? Warm things out.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He tried to freeze me AGAIN. I'm spicy now. He can't.
lines.script: [indignant, proud] He tried to freeze me AGAIN. [fierce, silly] I'm spicy now. He can't.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves. Nobody grows up. Nobody forgets a birthday.
lines.script: [cold, heavy] Good. Nothing changes. Nobody leaves. [low, brittle] Nobody grows up. Nobody forgets a birthday.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...Wait. Mr. Pistachio said. The DOOR.
lines.script: [halting, dawning] ...Wait. [hushed, excited] Mr. Pistachio said. The DOOR.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. He needs something on his door. Something that's HIS.
lines.script: [urgent, quick] Tah Tah. He needs something on his door. [sure, gentle] Something that's HIS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Okay. Presents are before cake. New rule.
lines.script: [thoughtful, dry] ...Okay. [decisive, warm] Presents are before cake. New rule.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: An INSTAX. Tata. A PRINTER. For PHOTOS.
lines.script: [squealing, awed] An INSTAX. Tah Tah. [breathless, thrilled] A PRINTER. For PHOTOS.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...The cab photo. This morning. All of us.
lines.script: [soft, remembering] ...The cab photo. [brightening, hushed] This morning. All of us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pair it to my phone. One tap. It's still on there.
lines.script: [quick, calm] Pair it to my phone. One tap. [reassuring, soft] It's still on there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Printing...
lines.script: [hushed, expectant] Printing...

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You don't have to freeze it. You just take a picture. See? It stays.
lines.script: [gentle, earnest] You don't have to freeze it. You just take a picture. [soft, sure] See? It stays.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's us. On your door. Happy birthday, Brain Freeze.
lines.script: [tender, warm] That's us. On your door. [soft, heartfelt] Happy birthday, Brain Freeze.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And the BANNER. Dad made it light up.
lines.script: [proud, bright] And the BANNER. [beaming, eager] Dad made it light up.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...It's warm. Why's the picture WARM.
lines.script: [stunned, small] ...It's warm. [wondering, cracking] Why's the picture WARM.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: My lid. My LID. It's OPENING.
lines.script: [panicked, creaking] My lid. My LID. [astonished, overwhelmed] It's OPENING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then it's round two. Birthday Wish is ready. All three of us.
lines.script: [triumphant, fierce] Then it's round two. [bold, bright] Birthday Wish is ready. All three of us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody ready? It's still her birthday.
lines.script: [calm, steady] Everybody ready? [dry, fond] It's still her birthday.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Nobody ever warmed me up before. Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.
lines.script: [soft, stunned] ...Nobody ever warmed me up before. [quiet, sincere] Take the scoops. [small, humble] They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Fine. FINE. Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.
lines.script: [gruff, embarrassed] Fine. FINE. [muttering, softened] Take the scoops. They're in the freezer. Where scoops go.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: All nine. Still perfect. And MOO-RIELLE. You were on a FREEZER. We'll talk about it later.
lines.script: [relieved, gleeful] All nine. Still perfect. [scolding, loving] And MOO-RIELLE. You were on a FREEZER. [airy, ominous] We'll talk about it later.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Pistachio says happy birthday. Twenty years late.
lines.script: [quiet, warm] Mr. Pistachio says happy birthday. [soft, rueful] Twenty years late.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...He remembered?
lines.script: [small, tender] ...He remembered?

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: Hum.
lines.script: [soft, content] Hum.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Come to my party.
lines.script: [warm, simple] Come to my party.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Nobody has ever... Is there cake?
lines.script: [hesitant, vulnerable] ...Nobody has ever... [shy, hopeful] Is there cake?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's a LOT of cake.
lines.script: [warm, dry] There's a LOT of cake.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: I'll bring the ice. I'm mostly ice.
lines.script: [shy, eager] I'll bring the ice. [dry, deadpan] I'm mostly ice.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He can sit next to the duck.
lines.script: [earnest, generous] He can sit next to the duck.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You got them? All nine? Tom, I could KISS you. I won't. I'm sweaty.
lines.script: [breathless, delighted] You got them? All nine? [warm, gushing] Tom, I could KISS you. [wry, teasing] I won't. I'm sweaty.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Cake is on the counter. Dairy free. I read the box nine times. With my glasses.
lines.script: [proud, fussing] Cake is on the counter. Dairy free. [emphatic, frazzled] I read the box nine times. [pointed, smug] With my glasses.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nine scoops. In my day we got one scoop. And a lecture.
lines.script: [nostalgic] Nine scoops. In my day we got one scoop. [dry, wry] And a lecture.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: My rock says happy birthday. He's on the counter. Please don't frost him.
lines.script: [soft, earnest] My rock says happy birthday. He's on the counter. [sincere, pleading] ...Please don't FROST him.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I brought a tree. A small one. It said it wanted to come.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy] I brought a tree. A small one. [serene, mellow] ...It said it wanted to come.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Twelve people, one duck, one cow. I counted twice. The freezer counts as a person.
lines.script: [crisp, rapid] Twelve people, one duck, one cow. I counted TWICE. [matter-of-fact, flat] ...The freezer counts as a person.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: I brought ice. Where do you want the ice.
lines.script: [flat, hesitant] I brought ice. [stiff, earnest] Where do you want the ice.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody told me there'd be a FREEZER at the table.
lines.script: [suspicious] Nobody told me there'd be a FREEZER at the table.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: He's a guest, Boppy. Sit. He can sit next to you. You could use the cold on that knee.
lines.script: [firm, sweet] He's a guest, Boppy. Sit. [practical, warm] He can sit next to you. [brisk, caring] You could use the cold on that knee.

lines.speaker: Mr. Pistachio
lines.text: Cones for everybody. And... hey, old friend. Happy birthday. I'm sorry it took twenty years.
lines.script: [booming, warm] Cones for everybody. [soft, sincere] And... hey, old friend. Happy birthday. [quiet, remorseful] I'm sorry it took twenty years.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...Hum.
lines.script: [quiet, overwhelmed] ...Hum.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: That's a happy hum.
lines.script: [soft, shy] That's a happy hum.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody, this is the Nine Scoop Sundae. Vanilla, strawberry, mint, chocolate, cookie dough, coffee, peanut butter, lemon, and black and white cookie on top.
lines.script: [proud, dry] Everybody, this is the Nine Scoop Sundae. [savoring, steady] Vanilla, strawberry, mint, chocolate, cookie dough, coffee, peanut butter, lemon, [pleased, warm] and black and white cookie on top.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Moo-rielle gets her own tiny scoop. Mint. She earned it.
lines.script: [tender, proud] Moo-rielle gets her own tiny scoop. [warm, firm] Mint. She earned it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Candles! Everybody sing! Grace, make a wish!
lines.script: [cheering, brisk] Candles! Everybody sing! [warm, excited] Grace, make a wish!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...I blew them out. The duck made me.
lines.script: [sheepish, small] ...I blew them out. [earnest, blaming] The duck made me.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ROSE.
lines.script: [outraged, shrieking] ROSE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Relight. Nine candles. Hold still, please.
lines.script: [dry, patient] Relight. Nine candles. [calm, gentle] Hold still, please.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Okay. For real this time. I wish...
lines.script: [solemn, hushed] Okay. For real this time. [slow, quiet] I wish...

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm not telling. That's the rule. I didn't make the rule.
lines.script: [coy, smug] I'm not telling. [pert, flat] That's the rule. I didn't make the rule.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Nine candles, one breath. I counted. Perfect score.
lines.script: [crisp, delighted] Nine candles, one breath. I counted. [deadpan, proud] ...Perfect score.

lines.speaker: Brain Freeze
lines.text: ...This is a good birthday. I'm putting it on my door.
lines.script: [quiet, content] ...This is a good birthday. [soft, shy] I'm putting it on my door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh! Penny called. She's got birthday things for you at the shop, Grace. Three of them. On the house.
lines.script: [bright, excited] Oh! Penny called. [warm, brisk] She's got birthday things for you at the shop, Grace. [teasing, pleased] Three of them. On the house.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A SASH? Is one of them a SASH?
lines.script: [breathless, hopeful] A SASH? [squealing, thrilled] Is one of them a SASH?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Go see. After cake.
lines.script: [warm, teasing] Go see. After cake.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hold on. It's your mom.
lines.script: [dry, bracing] Hold on. [wry] It's your mom.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. Don't panic. I'm panicking enough for both of us.
lines.script: [brisk, strained] Tom. Don't panic. [wry, high-strung] I'm panicking enough for both of us.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The invitations never went out. Justin was supposed to mail them Monday. Justin was at work Monday. Justin is at work now.
lines.script: [clipped, exasperated] The invitations never went out. Justin was supposed to mail them Monday. [flat, pointed] Justin was at work Monday. [weary] Justin is at work now.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Grace's friends are in the Square. Pip, Moss and Dot. Hand them out. By HAND. Like it's 1994.
lines.script: [brisk, coaching] Grace's friends are in the Square. Pip, Moss and Dot. Hand them out. [emphatic, firm] By HAND. [dry] Like it's 1994.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOM. It's fine. I'll invite them myself. I'm very persuasive.
lines.script: [bossy, unbothered] MOM. It's fine. [smug, airy] I'll invite them myself. I'm very persuasive.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You get that from me. Go. Love you. Scoops, friends, home by four.
lines.script: [proud, fond] You get that from me. Go. Love you. [quick, brisk] Scoops, friends, home by four.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I invite the duck?
lines.script: [hopeful, earnest] Can I invite the duck?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The duck is already coming. The duck is in your arms.
lines.script: [deadpan, amused] The duck is already coming. [dry, flat] The duck is in your arms.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Pip! My party. Today. Four o'clock. There's a sundae with NINE scoops.
lines.script: [bright, bossy] Pip! My party. Today. Four o'clock. [hushed, thrilled] There's a sundae with NINE scoops.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Can my rock come? He's never been to a party.
lines.script: [earnest, soft] Can my rock come? [solemn, sincere] He's NEVER been to a party.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: He gets nervous around cake. He'll be fine. He's a rock.
lines.script: [tender, reassuring] He gets nervous around cake. [sincere, plain] He'll be fine. ...He's a rock.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Rocks LOVE cake.
lines.script: [fierce, hushed] Rocks LOVE cake.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Then we'll be there. Both of us. He'll bring a gift. It's a smaller rock.
lines.script: [relieved, soft] Then we'll be there. BOTH of us. He'll bring a gift. [sincere, proud] ...It's a smaller rock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Three friends. Three scoops so far. I like threes.
lines.script: [pleased, crisp] Three friends. Three scoops so far. [fond, satisfied] I like threes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six scoops to go. North. Into the Hollow.
lines.script: [dry, rallying] Six scoops to go. [steady, calm] North. Into the Hollow.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Moss! Party. My house. Four. Bring nothing. Bring yourself.
lines.script: [bright, bossy] Moss! Party. My house. Four. [grand, warm] Bring nothing. Bring yourself.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I asked the tree if I should go.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy] I asked the tree if I should go.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: It said nothing. That means yes. Trees are very supportive.
lines.script: [slow, mellow] It said nothing. [unbothered, serene] That means yes. Trees are VERY supportive.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: Also, the tree says a freezer went north this morning. Humming. It wasn't happy.
lines.script: [low, drifting] Also, the tree says a freezer went north this morning. [slow, uneasy] Humming. [soft, sorry] It wasn't happy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank the tree for us.
lines.script: [dry, kind] Thank the tree for us.

lines.speaker: Moss
lines.text: I already did. It said nothing. Very gracious.
lines.script: [slow, content] I already did. It said nothing. [serene, pleased] ...Very gracious.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dot! My birthday party. Today. Will you come?
lines.script: [bright, hopeful] Dot! My birthday party. Today. [sweet, bossy] Will you come?

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Nine years. Nine scoops. Nine candles. That's twenty-seven nines. I'll be there.
lines.script: [crisp, delighted] Nine years. Nine scoops. Nine candles. [quick, proud] That's TWENTY-SEVEN nines. [flat, firm] I'll be there.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: I'll count the guests. Somebody has to.
lines.script: [brisk, dutiful] I'll count the guests. [matter-of-fact, flat] ...SOMEBODY has to.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Count the duck too.
lines.script: [earnest, insistent] Count the duck too.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: One duck. Counted.
lines.script: [deadpan, crisp] One duck. ...Counted.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: I'm taking my pet rock for a walk.
lines.script: [soft, proud] I'm taking my pet rock for a walk.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: He's shy. Please don't make eye contact.
lines.script: [hushed, protective] He's shy. [solemn, pleading] Please don't make eye contact.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Excellent. He's already learned 'stay'.
lines.script: [delighted, whispering] Excellent. He's ALREADY learned 'stay'.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I asked a tree for directions.
lines.script: [slow, dreamy] I asked a tree for directions.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: It said nothing. Very mysterious.
lines.script: [slow, amazed] It said nothing. [mellow, dreamy] ...VERY mysterious.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I think I'm barking up the wrong tree.
lines.script: [slow, smug] I think I'm barking up... the wrong tree.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Ten doors and THREE gaps in the trees now. Somebody opened one by the school.
lines.script: [crisp, excited] Ten doors and THREE gaps in the trees now. [scandalized, quick] SOMEBODY opened one by the school.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: I had to start all over. I'm at four hundred and six.
lines.script: [deflated, annoyed] I had to start ALL over. [flat, precise] ...I'm at four hundred and six.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: You got the tin back? Ten doors, two gaps, one pie tin. All accounted for.
lines.script: [brisk, pleased] You got the tin back? [proud, precise] Ten doors, two gaps, one pie tin. [crisp, satisfied] All accounted for.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: A mud blob ran through the Square with a pie tin. One blob. One tin. I counted.
lines.script: [fast, indignant] A mud blob ran through the Square with a pie tin. [matter-of-fact, precise] One blob. One tin. ...I counted.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: It went north. Into the gap in the trees. Gap number one.
lines.script: [crisp, certain] It went north. Into the gap in the trees. [precise, flat] Gap number one.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: This town has ten doors and two gaps in the trees.
lines.script: [quick, precise] This town has ten doors and two gaps in the trees.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: I've counted them seventeen times.
lines.script: [proud, precise] I've counted them SEVENTEEN times.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Tomorrow I'm moving on to windows.
lines.script: [deadpan, resolved] Tomorrow... I'm moving on to windows.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm training for the annual sit-down.
lines.script: [slow, dignified] I'm training for the annual sit-down.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: My coach is a bench.
lines.script: [deadpan, dignified] My coach... is a bench.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: We have a very supportive relationship.
lines.script: [deadpan, warm] We have a VERY supportive relationship.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: A mud blob just ran past me carrying a pie.
lines.script: [bright, amazed] A mud blob just ran past me... carrying a PIE.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I didn't stop it. I collect wrong turns, not pies.
lines.script: [breezy, unbothered] I didn't stop it. [matter-of-fact, cheerful] I collect wrong turns, not pies.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Boppy went by with a fishing rod and a jar of peppers.
lines.script: [chatty, bright] Boppy went by with a fishing rod and a jar of peppers.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: He was walking slower than me. Nobody walks slower than me. I collect slow walks too, now.
lines.script: [amazed, rambling] He was walking SLOWER than me. NOBODY walks slower than me. [sincere, cheerful] ...I collect slow walks too, now.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I'm not lost. I'm collecting wrong turns.
lines.script: [sunny, breezy] I'm not lost. [unbothered, proud] I'm COLLECTING wrong turns.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: That pond up north owes me an apology.
lines.script: [breezy, annoyed] That pond up north owes me an APOLOGY.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Long story. Short socks.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, breezy] Long story. ...Short socks.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Your father caught Old Iron-Gill? And let him GO? Forty years of telling that story, and now it's true.
lines.script: [amazed, slow] Your father caught Old Iron-Gill? And let him GO? [deadpan, dry] FORTY years of telling that story, and now it's true.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: He came by the shack this morning. The fish, not your father. Just floated there. I think he wanted to say hello.
lines.script: [quiet, amazed] He came by the shack this morning. [deadpan, dry] The fish, NOT your father. [soft, moved] Just floated there. I think he wanted to say hello.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: You saw it? Old Iron-Gill? Forty years I have run this shack. I thought it was a story.
lines.script: [hushed, incredulous] You saw it? Old Iron-Gill? [slow, weighty] Forty years I have run this shack. [small, wondering] I thought it was a story.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: It went west, into the marsh. The Whispering Marsh. The reeds talk out there. Mostly nonsense.
lines.script: [low, slow] It went west, into the marsh. The Whispering Marsh. The reeds talk out there. [deadpan, dismissive] ...Mostly nonsense.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Bait shack is open. Worms, minnows, and a sandwich I'm not selling.
lines.script: [dry, slow] Bait shack is open. [deadpan, flat] Worms, minnows, and a sandwich I'm NOT selling.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. He has caught nothing. Very consistent.
lines.script: [deadpan, fond] Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. [flat, tickled] He has caught nothing. [dry] Very consistent.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: They say a catfish lives out there older than the boards. I say they say a lot.
lines.script: [low, mischievous] They say a catfish lives out there older than the boards. [deadpan, skeptical] I say... they say a LOT.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Thirty parents. Zero tears. One very well-behaved pen. Best conference night in thirty-one years.
lines.script: [tired, deadpan] Thirty parents. Zero tears. ...One very well-behaved pen. [warm, proud] Best conference night in thirty-one years.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Come to Field Day, Tom. Amy runs the relay. Amy always runs the relay.
lines.script: [warm, level] Come to Field Day, Tom. Amy runs the relay. [deadpan, knowing] Amy ALWAYS runs the relay.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Conferences start at seven. SEVEN. The bells say otherwise. The bells are wrong.
lines.script: [stern, exasperated] Conferences start at seven. SEVEN. [deadpan, annoyed] The bells say otherwise. ...The bells are wrong.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Clear the rooms, set the hallway clocks to seven, and the Cafetorium will open. I hope.
lines.script: [brisk, hopeful] Clear the rooms, set the hallway clocks to seven, and the Cafetorium will open. [small, deadpan] ...I hope.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Principal Pruitt. Thirty-one years at Long Island Elementary. I've seen everything. Not tonight, though. Tonight is new.
lines.script: [proud, weary] Principal Pruitt. Thirty-one years at Long Island Elementary. I've seen EVERYTHING. [deadpan, low] Not tonight, though. ...Tonight is new.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Marco is reading at a third-grade level! Mrs. Gregori showed me the chart. There was a chart!
lines.script: [giddy, proud] Marco is reading at a third-grade level! Mrs. Gregori showed me the chart. [gleeful, amazed] There was a CHART!

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I cried a little. In the minivan. Don't tell Marco.
lines.script: [sheepish, tender] I cried a little. In the minivan. [hushed, sincere] ...Don't tell Marco.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: I'm Marco’s dad. Marco says Mrs. Gregori is the toughest teacher in the whole school.
lines.script: [friendly, chatty] I'm Marco’s dad. [amused, impressed] Marco says Mrs. Gregori is the TOUGHEST teacher in the whole school.

lines.speaker: bean
lines.text: Marco also says she's his favorite. Please don't tell Marco I told you.
lines.script: [warm, conspiratorial] Marco also says she's his favorite. [quick, whispering] PLEASE don't tell Marco I told you.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Thirty conferences, nine hundred cookies, one laminator. Everything went on schedule. MY schedule.
lines.script: [crisp, triumphant] Thirty conferences, nine hundred cookies, one laminator. [smug, prim] Everything went on schedule. ...MY schedule.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Tell Mrs. Gregori her bulletin board is the best in the building. Don't tell the other teachers.
lines.script: [hushed, conspiratorial] Tell Mrs. Gregori her bulletin board is the BEST in the building. [mischievous, hushed] ...Don't tell the other teachers.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Kowalski. PTA president. I brought nine hundred cookies and a laminator.
lines.script: [brisk, commanding] Kowalski. PTA president. [smug, flat] I brought nine hundred cookies... and a laminator.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The sign-up sheet RAN AWAY. On little paper legs. I've never been so offended.
lines.script: [scandalized, shrill] The sign-up sheet RAN AWAY. On little paper legs. [appalled, prim] I've NEVER been so offended.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: They fixed the bells! In my lifetime! I'm going to tell everyone at the diner.
lines.script: [delighted, amazed] They fixed the bells! In MY lifetime! [deadpan, eager] I'm going to tell EVERYONE at the diner.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm here for my grandson. He's in the second grade. I was in the second grade here in 1956.
lines.script: [slow, warm] I'm here for my grandson. He's in the second grade. [unhurried, wistful] I was in the second grade here... in 1956.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: The bells were wrong in 1956 too. Nobody fixed them. Things were simpler.
lines.script: [dry, unhurried] The bells were wrong in 1956 too. Nobody fixed them. [deadpan, fond] ...Things were simpler.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: Welcome! Our bread is emotionally available.
lines.script: [bubbly, bright] Welcome! [sincere, chirpy] Our bread is EMOTIONALLY available.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: The baguettes? A little crusty.
lines.script: [playful, teasing] The baguettes? [matter-of-fact, bright] ...A little crusty.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: Today's special is yesterday's tomorrow toast.
lines.script: [chipper, proud] Today's special is yesterday's... tomorrow toast.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: It's quiet. Properly quiet. The good kind. Thank you, Tom.
lines.script: [hushed, relieved] It's quiet. Properly quiet. The good kind. [whispering, warm] Thank you, Tom.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Story time is Saturdays now. The Unread asked for Grace. By name.
lines.script: [whispering, pleased] Story time is Saturdays now. [hushed, amazed] The Unread asked for Grace. ...By NAME.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: The Stacks are through the staff door. Please be careful. And please don't answer the books.
lines.script: [whispering, grave] The Stacks are through the staff door. Please be careful. [hushed, urgent] And please don't answer the books.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: I'm fine. Everything is fine. The dictionaries haven't slept in a week.
lines.script: [whispering, brittle] I'm fine. EVERYTHING is fine. [grave, haggard] The dictionaries haven't slept in a week.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: It's fine. Everything is fine. Please whisper.
lines.script: [whispering, strained] It's fine. Everything is fine. [hushed, sharp] PLEASE whisper.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: ...Did you hear that? That wasn't me. I'd know my own shush.
lines.script: [whispering, spooked] ...Did you hear that? That wasn't me. [deadpan, hushed] I'd know my OWN shush.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Please whisper. The dictionaries are sleeping.
lines.script: [whispering, prim] Please whisper. [hushed, deadpan] The dictionaries are sleeping.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Someone shelved a sandwich under 'S'.
lines.script: [whispering, scandalized] Someone shelved a sandwich... under 'S'.

lines.speaker: page
lines.text: Technically correct. Deeply concerning.
lines.script: [whispering, flat] Technically correct. ...DEEPLY concerning.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I name every plant here.
lines.script: [soft, tender] I name every plant here.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: They're all called Steve. It saves time.
lines.script: [gentle, serene] They're ALL called Steve. [soft, matter-of-fact] ...It saves time.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Except that one. That's Assistant Steve.
lines.script: [hushed, fond] Except that one. [serene, proud] That's ASSISTANT Steve.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: Your parcel is arriving any Tuesday now.
lines.script: [chipper, casual] Your parcel is arriving ANY Tuesday now.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: The snails asked for smaller uniforms.
lines.script: [cheery, offhand] The snails asked for... smaller uniforms.

lines.speaker: kit
lines.text: I deliver good news. Bad news has to walk.
lines.script: [bright, proud] I deliver good news. [matter-of-fact, breezy] Bad news has to WALK.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The kettle is still going on about that man in the long coat. Gold coins. Paying double.
lines.script: [gossipy, relishing] The kettle is STILL going on about that man in the long coat. [low, scandalized] Gold coins. Paying double.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: I told it to mind its own business. It's a kettle. It has no business.
lines.script: [prim, matter-of-fact] I told it to mind its own business. [deadpan, flat] It's a kettle. ...It HAS no business.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: The kettle has been gossiping again.
lines.script: [hushed, conspiratorial] The kettle has been gossiping... again.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: It spilled the tea. Literally.
lines.script: [delighted, mischievous] It spilled the tea. [matter-of-fact, pleased] ...Literally.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Please mind the dramatic biscuits.
lines.script: [prim, deadpan] Please mind the DRAMATIC biscuits.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: The moon is back. I looked at it for an hour. I didn't even write anything down.
lines.script: [soft, joyful] The moon is back. I looked at it for an HOUR. [dreamy, sheepish] I didn't even write anything down.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: I swept the club stairs. Twelve years of wondering, and it was just a very dusty party.
lines.script: [drifting, sheepish] I swept the club stairs. [soft, earnest] Twelve years of wondering, and it was just... a very DUSTY party.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: The door is open. Twelve years I have swept this floor, and that door is open.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] The door is open. [slow, weighty] Twelve years I have swept this floor, and that door is open.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: If you see the moon up there, please tell it to come home. My telescope misses it.
lines.script: [wistful, tender] If you see the moon up there, PLEASE tell it to come home. [small, sincere] ...My telescope misses it.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: There's supposed to be a full moon tonight. My telescope can't find it.
lines.script: [worried, soft] There's supposed to be a full moon tonight. [quiet, uneasy] My telescope can't find it.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: It's not behind a cloud. It's just not THERE. I checked four times.

lines.text: The desert was gorgeous. Lachlan found a rock. Isla ate a rock. Different rock.
lines.script: [breathless, wry] The desert was gorgeous. Lachlan found a rock. [deadpan, dry] Isla ate a rock. Different rock.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: MICHAEL. Can you grab Isla? She's going for the dog bowl.
lines.script: [sharp, urgent] MICHAEL. Can you grab Isla? [quick, alarmed] She's going for the dog bowl.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Tom! Hi! Sorry, I'm mid-sentence in my head. I'm filing a story on AI in classrooms.
lines.script: [bright, flustered] Tom! Hi! Sorry, I'm mid-sentence in my head. [quick, wry] I'm filing a story on AI in classrooms.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: The kids use it to write the homework. The teachers use it to grade the homework. Nobody is in the room.
lines.script: [fast, wry] The kids use it to write the homework. The teachers use it to grade the homework. [flat, pointed] Nobody is in the room.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: MICHAEL. Can you grab Isla? She has a leaf. She's going to eat the leaf.
lines.script: [sharp, calling] MICHAEL. Can you grab Isla? [rushed, alarmed] She has a leaf. She's going to eat the leaf.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: My editor wants a piece on AI taking jobs. I said I'd write it myself. While I still can.
lines.script: [wry, quick] My editor wants a piece on AI taking jobs. [dry, pointed] I said I'd write it myself. While I still can.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Michael, can you take Lachlan? He's licking the fence. Thank you, babe.
lines.script: [quick, distracted] Michael, can you take Lachlan? He's licking the fence. [warm, sweet] Thank you, babe.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Everybody asks if robots will take their jobs. I tell them a robot still can't fold a fitted sheet. Neither can I.
lines.script: [quick, wry] Everybody asks if robots will take their jobs. I tell them a robot still can't fold a fitted sheet. [dry, deadpan] Neither can I.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: I interviewed a chatbot today. It was very polite. Too polite. I didn't trust it.
lines.script: [wry, thoughtful] I interviewed a chatbot today. It was very polite. [suspicious, low] Too polite. I didn't trust it.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Michael! Isla is near the curb. Okay. Never mind. Thank you, babe.
lines.script: [sharp, alarmed] Michael! Isla is near the curb. [relieved, warm] Okay. Never mind. Thank you, babe.

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Did Nara eat today? Tell me the truth. Michael, did Nara eat?
lines.script: [anxious, pleading] Did Nara eat today? Tell me the truth. [urgent, louder] Michael, did Nara eat?

lines.speaker: olivia
lines.text: Teachers aren't getting replaced. They're getting a very confident new student who never did the reading.
lines.script: [wry, sharp] Teachers aren't getting replaced. [dry, amused] They're getting a very confident new student who never did the reading.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Best potluck ever. Lachlan fell asleep in the bread basket.
lines.script: [calm, deadpan] Best potluck ever. [dry, tender] Lachlan fell asleep in the bread basket.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Cold lasagna, one diaper bag, and Isla eating the tablecloth. We're thriving.
lines.script: [tired, dry] Cold lasagna, one diaper bag, and Isla eating the tablecloth. [deadpan, cheerful] We're thriving.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Lachlan got his truck back. He hasn't put it down. He's eating cereal with one hand.
lines.script: [low, tender] Lachlan got his truck back. He hasn't put it down. [dry, amused] He's eating cereal with one hand.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Zero car keys and one very sticky toddler. Wait. Keys. Gutter. Right.
lines.script: [tired, deadpan] Zero car keys and one very sticky toddler. [slow, dawning] Wait... Keys. Gutter. Right.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Hey, Tom. Good to see you. Please ignore the cracker crumbs. They live here now.
lines.script: [warm, tired] Hey, Tom. Good to see you. [dry, deadpan] Please ignore the cracker crumbs. They live here now.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I work at Meta. I build things that connect people. Right now I'm connecting a four-year-old to a nap.
lines.script: [calm, deadpan] I work at Meta. I build things that connect people. [dry, worn] Right now I'm connecting a four-year-old to a nap.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I heard Olivia say Michael. Whatever it is, I'm on it. Isla, that is not a snack.
lines.script: [calm, dry] I heard Olivia say Michael. Whatever it is, I'm on it. [gentle, firm] Isla, that is not a snack.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Yes, Olivia. Heard you. Handled. Lachlan, we do not lick the fence.
lines.script: [patient, deadpan] Yes, Olivia. Heard you. Handled. [mild, firm] Lachlan, we do not lick the fence.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Lachlan wants to know if Nara is his dog. I said it's complicated. It's not. It's his dog.
lines.script: [dry, tired] Lachlan wants to know if Nara is his dog. I said it's complicated. [soft, certain] It's not. It's his dog.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Isla said her first word last week. It was no. She uses it very well.
lines.script: [deadpan, proud] Isla said her first word last week. [dry] It was no. [amused, warm] She uses it very well.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I took a meeting today with Isla on my lap. She muted me. Best meeting of the quarter.
lines.script: [dry, weary] I took a meeting today with Isla on my lap. She muted me. [deadpan, tickled] Best meeting of the quarter.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: My arms have never been stronger. I haven't lifted a weight in four years.
lines.script: [flat, proud] My arms have never been stronger. [deadpan, dry] I haven't lifted a weight in four years.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for mine. Nobody wants bedtime.
lines.script: [calm, wry] Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for mine. [deadpan, tired] Nobody wants bedtime.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Mr. Washington is solid amber, mid-sentence, one finger raised. A tiny chip of gold sits on the brim of his hat.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] Mr. Washington is solid amber, mid-sentence, one finger raised. [soft, wondering] A tiny chip of gold sits on the brim of his hat.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Whatever 1979 story he was telling is still in there. Still warm.
lines.script: [hushed, tender] Whatever 1979 story he was telling is still in there. [soft, warm] Still warm.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...and that’s why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Did I fall asleep? Again?
lines.script: [slow, groggy] ...and THAT’s why you never trust a Tuesday. [flat, sheepish] Hm? Did I fall asleep? ...Again?

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Back in 1979, nobody got stuck on a sentence. Well. Harold did.
lines.script: [slow, fond] Back in 1979, NOBODY got stuck on a sentence. [deadpan, dry] Well. ...Harold did.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: That coat looks right on you. My daddy would say so. Then he'd say stand up straight.
lines.script: [warm, slow] That coat looks right on you. My daddy would say so. [dry, amused] Then he'd say... stand up straight.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Forty loaves. I ate four. Don't tell Bernadette.
lines.script: [slow, confiding] Forty loaves. ...I ate four. [low, mischievous] Don't tell Bernadette.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Forty years I've made gumbo for this potluck. Today the stove won't light. The flame just leans. Toward the boulevard.
lines.script: [slow, worried] FORTY years I've made gumbo for this potluck. Today the stove won't light. [hushed, uneasy] The flame just leans. ...Toward the boulevard.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: My daddy drove the 7 line out of the old Car Barn. He said the stove down there could warm a whole street.
lines.script: [warm, nostalgic] My daddy drove the 7 line out of the old Car Barn. [fond, proud] He said the stove down there could warm a WHOLE street.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: My reading glasses! Found in a hole in the park. I won't ask.
lines.script: [delighted, surprised] My reading glasses! Found in a hole in the park. [unhurried, dry] ...I won't ask.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Back in 1979 the squirrels were polite. They waited until you finished your sandwich.
lines.script: [slow, matter-of-fact] Back in 1979 the squirrels were POLITE. [dry, flat] They waited until you finished your sandwich.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Somebody took my reading glasses off the porch rail. I have read the same headline for three days.
lines.script: [grumbling, annoyed] Somebody took my reading glasses off the porch rail. [weary, deadpan] I have read the same headline for THREE days.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: I think it says WEATHER. It might say WHETHER.
lines.script: [slow, uncertain] I think it says WEATHER. [unhurried, flat] ...It might say WHETHER.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Back in 1979, this whole block...
lines.script: [slow, drowsy] Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon. Nobody needs to get any older.
lines.script: [drowsy, content] Such a nice afternoon. [soft, wishful] It should always be this afternoon. [gentle, slow] Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Where was I? Oh. 1979. This whole block smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night.
lines.script: [slow, groggy] Where was I? Oh. 1979. [warm, savoring] This whole block smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: That smog had me stuck on one sentence for an hour. At my age I don't have hours to spare.
lines.script: [slow, weary] That smog had me stuck on ONE sentence for an hour. [dry, flat] At my age... I don't have hours to spare.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Thank you, Tom. And your young man. And the dog. Especially the dog.
lines.script: [warm, heartfelt] Thank you, Tom. And your young man. [deadpan, fond] And the dog. ...ESPECIALLY the dog.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Bought this house in 1979. Same porch, same chair, same view.
lines.script: [slow, contented] Bought this house in 1979. [dry, settled] Same porch, same chair, same view.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: Back then you could hear zydeco from the boulevard on a Saturday night.
lines.script: [fond, wistful] Back then you could hear zydeco from the boulevard on a Saturday night.

lines.speaker: washington
lines.text: You're the one fixing up the green house? Keep the old windows. They're better than the new ones.
lines.script: [warm, curious] You're the one fixing up the green house? [low, firm] KEEP the old windows. They're better than the new ones.

lines.speaker: Marisol
lines.text: Marisol is amber from her shoulders to her sneakers. The leash runs from her hand to a very loyal dog. The dog is free. The dog is sitting beside her. He didn’t leave.
lines.script: [hushed, tender] Marisol is amber from her shoulders to her sneakers. The leash runs from her hand to a very loyal dog. [soft, gladdened] The dog is free. The dog is sitting beside her. [gentle, moved] He didn’t leave.

lines.speaker: Marisol
lines.text: The color’s back! My dog’s back! He never left! He was just being loyal. Look at him. So loyal.
lines.script: [overjoyed, relieved] The color’s back! My dog’s back! [fond, proud] He never left! He was just being loyal. [melting, soft] Look at him. So loyal.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: My dog ate a whole loaf. I found him. He was under the table. He's always under the table.
lines.script: [dry, tired] My dog ate a WHOLE loaf. I found him. [deadpan, fond] He was under the table. ...He's ALWAYS under the table.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: My tamales are cold. My dog is cold. My dog is somewhere. He's probably cold.
lines.script: [deadpan, drifting] My tamales are cold. My dog is cold. [flat, unsure] My dog is... somewhere. He's PROBABLY cold.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Eleven tennis balls! Back! My dog is beside himself. Wherever he is.
lines.script: [delighted, breathless] ELEVEN tennis balls! Back! My dog is beside himself. [deadpan, flat] ...Wherever he is.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Every tennis ball on the block. Gone. My dog has nothing to ignore now.
lines.script: [mournful, dry] Every tennis ball on the block. Gone. [deadpan, flat] My dog has NOTHING to ignore now.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: There he is. No. That's a squirrel. It's looking at me.
lines.script: [hopeful, quick] There he is. [deadpan, uneasy] No. That's a squirrel. ...It's LOOKING at me.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: I'm walking my dog. I've always been walking my dog.
lines.script: [calm, vacant] I'm walking my dog. [soft, certain] I've always been walking my dog.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: I'll always be walking my dog. Isn't that nice?
lines.script: [serene, dreamy] I'll always be walking my dog. [soft, pleased] Isn't that nice?

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: I'm walking my dog. He's somewhere.
lines.script: [distracted, mild] I'm walking my dog. [deadpan, unbothered] He's... somewhere.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: My grandparents rented on this block. Now I rent on this block. We're a tradition.
lines.script: [dry, easygoing] My grandparents rented on this block. Now I rent on this block. [deadpan, proud] ...We're a TRADITION.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: There he is. No. That's a lemon.
lines.script: [hopeful, bright] There he is. [deadpan, deflated] No. ...That's a lemon.

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: Larry is amber, leaf blower raised. One leaf hangs in the air in front of him. After all these years it is finally perfectly still.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] Larry is amber, leaf blower raised. One leaf hangs in the air in front of him. [soft, wondering] After all these years it is finally perfectly still.

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: The leaf landed. It LANDED. I’ve been blowing that leaf since the smog. Thank you.
lines.script: [overcome, slow] The leaf landed. It LANDED. [tired, deadpan] I’ve been blowing that leaf since the smog. [warm, sincere] ...Thank you.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm blowing leaves. They're frosty. In LA. I have questions.
lines.script: [deadpan, puzzled] I'm blowing leaves. They're frosty. In LA. [flat, suspicious] ...I have questions.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm blowing leaves. The squirrels keep blowing them back.
lines.script: [weary, dignified] I'm blowing leaves. [deadpan, defeated] The squirrels keep blowing them BACK.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: It's a whole system. Their system is better.
lines.script: [grudging, slow] It's a whole system. [deadpan, dignified] ...Their system is BETTER.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm blowing leaves. The same leaf. Over and over.
lines.script: [flat, droning] I'm blowing leaves. [slow, hollow] The same leaf. Over... and over.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: It never lands. It never has to. Very peaceful.
lines.script: [drifting, content] It never lands. It never has to. [serene, slow] Very peaceful.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm blowing leaves.
lines.script: [deadpan, dignified] I'm blowing leaves.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Onto the next yard.
lines.script: [deadpan, brisk] Onto the next yard.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Tomorrow, they blow them back. It's a whole system.
lines.script: [patient, matter-of-fact] Tomorrow, they blow them back. [deadpan, accepting] ...It's a whole system.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Ray here. Shoot wrapped. Nobody got past me. Except the megaphone. And the moths. And the dog.
lines.script: [tired, proud] Ray here. Shoot wrapped. NOBODY got past me. [deadpan, sheepish] Except the megaphone. ...And the moths. [mumbling, low] ...And the dog.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Good job, Tom. Don't tell anyone I said good job.
lines.script: [low, grudging] Good job, Tom. [deadpan, warning] Don't tell anyone I said good job.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Nobody came through my gate. Nobody with legs.
lines.script: [proud, slow] NOBODY came through my gate. [deadpan, flat] ...Nobody with legs.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Little things, though. Buzzing. Clapping. One of them asked me for a compliment. I said no. I regret it.
lines.script: [low, deadpan] Little things, though. Buzzing. Clapping. One of them asked me for a compliment. [flat, heavy] I said no. ...I regret it.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Tom. Plus one dog. Plus one boyfriend who already works here. Fine. Go on in.
lines.script: [deadpan, slow] Tom. Plus one dog. Plus one boyfriend who ALREADY works here. [resigned, flat] ...Fine. Go on in.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Nobody gets past Ray. Except the dog. The dog got past Ray. Don't tell anyone.
lines.script: [proud, flat] NOBODY gets past Ray. [guilty, lower] Except the dog. The dog got past Ray. [hushed, pleading] ...Don't tell anyone.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: Craft services! Take a bagel. Take two. Nobody is counting. I'm counting.
lines.script: [bright, chirpy] Craft services! Take a bagel. Take two. NOBODY is counting. [quick, offhand] ...I'm counting.

lines.speaker: bun
lines.text: The crew eats like a swarm of locusts. Polite locusts. With lanyards.
lines.script: [cheerful, amused] The crew eats like a swarm of locusts. [prim, matter-of-fact] POLITE locusts. ...With lanyards.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: We WRAPPED! On time! Well. Four hours late. Which is on time for us.
lines.script: [exhausted, triumphant] We WRAPPED! On time! [matter-of-fact, rapid] Well. ...Four hours late. Which is on time for US.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: I'm going to sleep for a week. In my car. With the headset on.
lines.script: [spent, dreamy] I'm going to sleep for a WEEK. [flat, mumbling] In my car. ...With the headset on.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Rack two is still missing. Forty costumes. The actors are filming in bathrobes.
lines.script: [frazzled, rapid] Rack two is STILL missing. Forty costumes. [deadpan, defeated] ...The actors are filming in bathrobes.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Last thing on my radio before the static was the Stage 7 fog machine. It turned itself on.
lines.script: [spooked, clipped] Last thing on my radio before the static was the Stage 7 fog machine. [low, ominous] ...It turned ITSELF on.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Kiki. Production assistant. I have a headset, three radios and zero answers.
lines.script: [crisp, frazzled] Kiki. Production assistant. [matter-of-fact, rapid] I have a headset, three radios and ZERO answers.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: If anybody asks, I'm walking somewhere important. I'm always walking somewhere important.
lines.script: [hushed, hurried] If anybody asks, I'm walking somewhere important. [flat, proud] I'm ALWAYS walking somewhere important.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: We got the shot. All of them. Even the one with the horse.
lines.script: [relieved, giddy] We got the shot. ALL of them. [incredulous, deadpan] ...Even the one with the horse.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Tell TNB the costumes looked incredible. Tell him I said incredible. Tell him twice.
lines.script: [warm, urgent] Tell TNB the costumes looked incredible. Tell him I said INCREDIBLE. [deadpan, quick] ...Tell him twice.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Without wardrobe there's no shoot. Without a shoot there's no movie.
lines.script: [earnest, grateful] Without wardrobe there's no shoot. Without a shoot there's no movie.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Without a movie I go back to directing car commercials. I love cars. I don't love talking cars.
lines.script: [sarcastic, sinking] Without a movie I go back to directing car commercials. [wistful, tired] I love cars. [deadpan, flat] I DON't love... talking cars.

lines.speaker: la_woman
lines.text: Dana Park. Director. First feature. Please don't ask me how it's going.
lines.script: [weary, brisk] Dana Park. Director. First feature. [tense, deadpan] PLEASE don't ask me how it's going.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Case closed. I've filed my report. With myself. I approved it.
lines.script: [smug, officious] Case closed. I've filed my report. [deadpan, pleased] With myself. ...I approved it.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: I said they were organized. Nobody believed me. Write that down.
lines.script: [smug, sharp] I SAID they were organized. Nobody believed me. [officious, clipped] ...Write that down.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: You're a good neighbor, Tom. So is the dog. Mostly the dog.
lines.script: [warm, approving] You're a good neighbor, Tom. So is the dog. [flat, dry] ...MOSTLY the dog.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: The lookouts first. Playground, garden, picnic tables. Then that dog of yours digs.
lines.script: [brisk, authoritative] The lookouts first. Playground, garden, picnic tables. [knowing, pointed] Then that dog of yours digs.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Then the tree. There's a knock. I have only ever heard parts of it.
lines.script: [hushed, ominous] Then the tree. There's a knock. [annoyed, quieter] I have only ever heard PARTS of it.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Bernadette. Neighborhood Watch Captain, nineteen years. Nothing gets past me.
lines.script: [crisp, proud] Bernadette. Neighborhood Watch Captain, nineteen years. [smug, firm] NOTHING gets past me.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Except squirrels. I'm working on it.
lines.script: [grave, sheepish] Except squirrels. [annoyed, muttering] ...I'm working on it.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: Welcome to Golden Hour. Every hour is golden hour if you believe.
lines.script: [dreamy, serene] Welcome to Golden Hour. [soft, sincere] EVERY hour is golden hour... if you believe.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: Our oat milk is oat-adjacent.
lines.script: [airy, unbothered] Our oat milk is oat-ADJACENT.

lines.speaker: luna
lines.text: Your name is Tom? I wrote TAM. It's basically the same.
lines.script: [sweet, oblivious] Your name is Tom? I wrote TAM. [dreamy, earnest] ...It's basically the same.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.text: Irasshaimase! Welcome!
lines.script: [booming, welcoming] Irasshaimase! Welcome!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.text: Tom-san, your Japanese is very good.
lines.script: [warm, kind] Tom-san, your Japanese is very good.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.text: It's not. But you're trying very hard, and I respect that.
lines.script: [blunt, gentle] It's not. [warm, respectful] But you're trying VERY hard, and I respect that.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Welcome. Breathe in. Now order.
lines.script: [calm, soothing] Welcome. Breathe in. [matter-of-fact, firm] ...Now order.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: We opened in March. The pupuseria next door has been here since 1994. We're learning a lot.
lines.script: [serene, mild] We opened in March. The pupuseria next door has been here since 1994. [calm, soft] ...We're learning a LOT.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Today's special is celery. Doña Carmen says that's not a meal. She's right.
lines.script: [calm, soothing] Today's special is celery. [serene, matter-of-fact] Doña Carmen says that's not a meal. ...She's right.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Welcome to Nickel's. I'm Penny's cousin. Better weather, same prices.
lines.script: [bright, brisk] Welcome to Nickel's. I'm Penny's cousin. [deadpan, breezy] Better weather, same prices.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Gear for the whole family, snacks for fights, sunscreen for the soul.
lines.script: [quick, chipper] Gear for the whole family, snacks for fights, [matter-of-fact, grand] sunscreen for the SOUL.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Got something to sell? I buy almost anything. Penny warned me about Steve.
lines.script: [eager, coaxing] Got something to sell? I buy almost ANYTHING. [hushed, suspicious] ...Penny warned me about Steve.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Back again! Did you find parking? Nobody finds parking.
lines.script: [bright, delighted] Back again! Did you find parking? [offhand, flat] ...NOBODY finds parking.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Browse all you like. Browsing is free in Los Angeles. Nothing else is.
lines.script: [breezy, bright] Browse all you like. Browsing is free in Los Angeles. [flat, knowing] ...Nothing else is.

lines.speaker: penny
lines.text: Fresh stock. Same Nickel.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] Fresh stock. Same Nickel.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: Backlot Wardrobe. If it was worn on screen, it lived here first.
lines.script: [proud, grand] Backlot Wardrobe. [cozy, knowing] If it was worn on screen, it lived here first.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: You're Tom? TNB's Tom! He found a shoe for us once. A lead actor's shoe. Four minutes before the take.
lines.script: [delighted, gossipy] You're Tom? TNB's Tom! He found a shoe for us once. A lead actor's shoe. [hushed, amazed] ...FOUR minutes before the take.

lines.speaker: oolong
lines.text: We still talk about the shoe. Tell him there's always a rack here with his name on it.
lines.script: [fond, solemn] We STILL talk about the shoe. [warm, insistent] Tell him there's always a rack here with his name on it.

lines.speaker: dolores
lines.text: Welcome to the Starlite. Built in 1931. The popcorn is newer. A little.
lines.script: [grand, slow] Welcome to the Starlite. Built in 1931. [cool, dry] The popcorn is newer. ...A little.

lines.speaker: dolores
lines.text: I have run the projector here for forty years. I've seen every movie twice.
lines.script: [slow, dignified] I have run the projector here for FORTY years. [arch, amused] I've seen every movie... twice.

lines.speaker: dolores
lines.text: Tonight it's a horror double feature. Your boyfriend would love it. You'd watch it through your fingers.
